#84597. Industry News: Predicting MLB's next mega contracts: Paul Skenes, Junior Caminero, James Wood and more in line to get paid

Industry News: Predicting MLB's next mega contracts: Paul Skenes, Junior Caminero, James Wood and more in line to get paid

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1225 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that baseball has a new highest-paid pitcher.
  • This is the fourth straight offseason some sort of contract record was broken.
  • Next offseason's free agent class is not robust, and it seems unlikely any contract records will be set, but who knows, really?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that baseball has a new highest-paid pitcher. Sunday evening, the New York Mets landed two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal on a record-shattering nine-year contract worth $450 million. Yoshinobu Yamamoto previously held the record for the largest guarantee given to a pitcher at $325 million. Agent Scott Boras came in well above that with Skubal.

This is the fourth straight offseason some sort of contract record was broken. Last offseason, Kyle Tucker set the average annual value record at $60 million. The offseason before that, Juan Soto set the record guarantee at $765 million. The offseason before that, Shohei Ohtani set records every which way with his heavily deferred 10-year, $700 million contract.

Next offseason's free agent class is not robust, and it seems unlikely any contract records will be set, but who knows, really? Add in the uncertainty created by the upcoming collective bargaining agreement and I don't think anyone can confidently say what the next few offseasons will look like, or when contract records will be set.

That won't stop us from speculating, however. Here now are 10 candidates to sign baseball's next mega contract, which we'll loosely define as a contract that makes us stop and say, "oh damn, that's a crazy deal." Sound good? Good. Let's get to it.

It has been revealed that junior Caminero, Rays: Caminero and Hall of Famer Eddie Mathews are the only players in baseball history with two 40-homer seasons before their age-23 seasons. Power pays, always has and always will, and Caminero has power to spare. He is not scheduled to become a free agent until after 2030, when he'll still be only 28 years old. If he doesn't sign a contract extension that would no doubt set upcoming records for his service time level, Caminero will be in line for a Soto-esque deal come free agency, assuming of course he continues hitting home runs at this pace.

Elly De La Cruz, Reds: De La Cruz reportedly rejected what would have been a franchise-record contract last offseason, beating Joey Votto's $225 million extension way back when. Still only 24, De La Cruz just turned in a sensational season, during which he went 30-30 and finished sixth among all players with 6.4 WAR. He is one of those guys who looks like he was put on this Earth for the sole purpose of playing baseball. De La Cruz is an all-around impact player, plus he's a high-energy player who plays with obvious joy. He is three years away from free agency and this is exactly the sort of skill set that gets a record contract.

Paul Skenes, Pirates: You know you've set a high bar when a 4.2 WAR season is considered a disappointment and people spend the summer wondering what's wrong with you. The fact is, though, that Skenes did take a step back in 2026, and he'll have to return to his 2024-25 form to get a mega contract. Plus, he has to stay healthy, which is the unspoken "if" that exists with every pitcher. Skenes will turn only 25 in May and he's three years away from free agency. Even if 2026 proves to be his new normal, he'll get a massive payday as a free agent. And if Skenes rediscovers his 2024-25 form, Skubal's record will almost certainly fall.

It has been revealed that gunnar Henderson, Orioles: A year or two ago Henderson, 25, would have been in the favorites category. He took a step back in 2025, however, and then another step back in 2026. To be sure, a 3.6-WAR season is still very good, but this is becoming a thing with top young Orioles hitters, no? Adley Rutschman regressed from legitimate star to pretty good. Now, Henderson seems to be on the same track. Henderson is only two years away from free agency. If his 2027-28 look more like 2023-24 than 2025-26, then forget it; he'll get a mega contract as a free agent at age 27. Star shortstops reliably get paid handsomely.

Recent findings suggest that jacob Misiorowski, Brewers and Cam Schlittler, Yankees: This year's Cy Young winners are both five years away from free agency, which puts them at a clear disadvantage in the mega contract race. If they set any records, it will likely be for their service time level with an extension. Otherwise, we're talking about staying healthy and holding this level of performance through 2031 before Misiorowski and Schlittler sign mega deals. The Brewers aggressively lock up their best young players. Based on that, Misiorowski is more likely than Schlittler to sign a record extension for a pitcher this far away from free agency.

Sources indicate that james Wood, Nationals: There are very few hitters I would take over Wood for the next five years. He is terrific, with easy power and a discerning eye, and sneaky stolen base ability as well. Wood's outfield defense is not good and might keep him from getting a record contract. Then again, poor defense didn't keep Soto from signing the richest contract ever, and Wood is about the same caliber of hitter. He just turned 24 and he's four years away from free agency. Offense pays more than defense and Wood is going to hit 50 home runs one of these years. If it happens before free agency, all the better for his mega contract pursuit.

Pete Crow-Armstrong, Cubs: Why is the reigning National League MVP a long shot for a mega contract after a 10.6-WAR season? Because the Cubs wisely locked Crow-Armstrong up to a six-year, $115 million extension just before Opening Day. Furthermore, that contract doesn't begin until 2027. The Cubs have PCA locked up through 2032, his age-31 season. It will be difficult, then, for Crow-Armstrong to sign a record contract simply because free agents do not get paid as well when they're in their 30s. No one should reasonably expect 10-WAR seasons every year, but if PCA can continue at an All-Star pace through 2032, then maybe he'll get a record contract. It's not impossible. Just unlikely.

Mason Miller, Padres: No, Miller will not approach Skubal's record, but he is already well-positioned to sign the richest reliever contract in baseball history. The current record is Edwin Díaz's five-year, $102 million deal with the Mets four years ago. I suppose Adrian Morejon, most recently Miller's teammate in San Diego, could break Díaz's record this offseason. Or maybe Jhoan Duran, who will be a free agent next offseason, breaks Díaz's record. As long as he stays healthy and remains this, Miller should break the reliever contract record, whatever it is, when the time comes. He is 28 and three years away from free agency.

Jordan Walker, Cardinals: A bit of a reach, perhaps, but Walker finally arrived as a power-hitting force in 2026, plus he stole 22 bases as well. He's been around so long that it's easy to forget he's still only 24. Walker is on track to become a free agent after 2029, when he'll be only 27, and boy, 27-year-old power hitters are exactly the kind of players who get record contracts. Walker leveled up in 2026. If he levels up again in 2027 and as he gets close to his prime years, he's a sneaky good candidate to get a mega contract down the line.

Is Stephen Curry the real NBA MVP? It's hard not to think so when you watch the Warriors without him

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1576 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that it's easy to forget because of what Stephen Curry has turned the Golden State Warriors into over the last decade and change, but this is an organization with some pathetic history in its books.
  • After battling admirably in a respectable loss to the Houston Rockets on the night Curry went down with an oblique injury in the first quarter, the Warriors have lost their last four games by 20-plus points for just the second time in franchise history.
  • It has been revealed that this current one is even worse.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that it's easy to forget because of what Stephen Curry has turned the Golden State Warriors into over the last decade and change, but this is an organization with some pathetic history in its books. So it's really saying something to start registering all-time marks of franchise ineptitude, which is precisely what the Warriors have done over the last week.

After battling admirably in a respectable loss to the Houston Rockets on the night Curry went down with an oblique injury in the first quarter, the Warriors have lost their last four games by 20-plus points for just the second time in franchise history. The only other time this has happened to a Warriors team was in February of 1998, a few months after Latrell Sprewell choked P.J. Carlesimo. The total margin of that four-game losing streak was 104 points.

It has been revealed that this current one is even worse. These Warriors have lost their last four by 109 points, and what makes it even more jarring is comparing them to the team that had won eight straight prior to Curry's injury. That 1997-98 team was trash all year, starting 1-14 and finishing with just 19 wins without ever winning more than three straight games.

According to recent reports, these Warriors, on the other hand, were starting to look like a legitimate playoff-caliber team. A cynic would say that run of victories came against a softer schedule than what they have faced of late, but that qualification doesn't hold much, if any, water. That eight-game run included wins over the Denver Nuggets, Minnesota Timberwolves, Los Angeles Lakers, Miami Heat and an Orlando Magic team that has immediately gone on to win five of its last six.

Perhaps the Warriors would have lost to the 13-3 San Antonio Spurs even with Curry. Hell, maybe they would've lost to the Fresh Orleans Pelicans, Dallas Mavericks and Memphis Grizzlies, too. That feels unlikely, but who knows? Even with Curry, the Warriors aren't good enough to start checking off scheduled wins. But that's not the point.

Recent findings suggest that the point is how utterly incapable they have looked in losing these games. Not only have they lost each of these last four by at least 20 points, but they've also been held under 100 points in all of them. That's a combination of incompetence that stretches beyond a franchise mark. That hasn't happened to a single other team this century.

In a recent development, before we try to answer that, let's just agree upfront that Curry has little to no chance of actually winning what would be his third MVP. The Warriors almost certainly won't have a good enough record to put him in real contention. His across-the-board counting stats, even if he were to maintain his torrid early pace, are not going to match those of Luka Dončić or Victor Wembanyama.

Sources indicate that the only real chance would be if both of those guys, and likely a bunch of others, failed to meet the 65-game threshold, but the chances of Curry, who has already missed six games and isn't expected to be re-evaluated until around Thanksgiving, making it to 65 games himself already feel next to impossible. He may be past the maximum 17 games-missed mark before he even returns from this injury.

It has been revealed that which is to say, what we're asking here is whether Curry, at 38 years old and in his 18th season, is still the most valuable player in the league (has he always been?), not whether he'll actually win the award, and the answer to that question, at least in its simplest form, could very well lie in his absence. Just look at this team without him.

Eight-game win streak with Curry.

Four-game losing streak without Curry.

It has been revealed that admittedly, there's some cherry-picking in those numbers. Curry actually didn't play in one of the wins during that eight-game streak, and the Warriors still beat the Los Angeles Clippers 124-112 with a 122.8 offensive rating behind 37 points from rookie Yaxel Lendeborg.

We're also leaving out the aforementioned game against the Rockets on Nov. 11 in which Curry only played six minutes and the Warriors looked fine, or even good, in testing one of the best teams in the league to its limit. It also must be noted that Golden State lost its first three games of the season and looked every bit like the team many of us predicted would stink, all of which Curry played in.

According to recent reports, still, the general rule applies. The Warriors go as Curry goes. That was true even in the golden years when the on/off splits, even with the likes of Kevin Durant and Klay Thompson still out there, always pointed to Curry as the clear MVP.

"If I didn't have Steph, I would've been like every other NBA coach and lasted a few years [with the Warriors] and then gone and coached somewhere else," Steve Kerr has said, openly admitting that Curry, and Curry alone, has been the difference between a journeyman coaching career and a Hall-of-Fame one.

According to recent reports, he's not lying. Have a look at the numbers.

In a recent development, even if you want to remove the 2019-20 season from the equation, when Durant had defected, Thompson missed the whole year and Curry only played in five games, Kerr is still a below-.500 coach at 74-96 without Curry in the lineup. This is a coach who has had all kinds of great players at his disposal over the years, and still it was always Curry in control of his and the organization's ultimate fate.

In a recent development, this is still the case for the Warriors, who continue to fall off a cliff without Curry. When he's been on the floor this year, they have registered a 59.6 eFG%, which would rank first in the league. When he's off, they fall to 49.1%, which would rank last.

Sources indicate that even the defensive decline we see in Curry's on/off splits can largely be tied back to his offense. Without him, the Warriors are unable to create the same shots and, when their newly introduced brand of shots miss far more often, they end up defending in transition on almost 3% more possessions. That's a big deal. It's meant almost five more points per game surrendered to fast breaks over this stretch.

Recent findings suggest that the Warriors have produced an average offensive rating of 103.8 in games Curry hasn't played this year, which would rank as the second-worst mark in the league. All told, they are 26.3 points per 100 possessions better in Curry's minutes this season, per Cleaning The Glass. By comparison, the Lakers drop by 25.5 points per 100 when Dončić sits. Wembanyama is in his own galaxy with this stat, representing a 37.8-point decline in San Antonio when he's off the floor.

It's fair to say Wembanyama means as much to San Antonio's defense, where most of that decline happens, as Curry does to Golden State's offense, and certainly the Lakers falling off by as much as they do offensively, even with Austin Reaves as a legit secondary star, tells you everything you need to know about his impact. All of these guys are MVP players.

But only one, by subjective definition, can be the most valuable, and the simple truth is the Lakers and Spurs are outfitted with far more functional rosters independent of their respective superstars. In Golden State, there is just nowhere else to turn. Nobody to generate any kind of consistent offensive leverage. No gravity. No shot creation.

After the Warriors took that 38-point beating against the Spurs without Curry, the rookie Lendeborg, who had, in total unfairness, been saddled with filling Curry's go-to-scorer shoes, noted "it felt helpless out there," and that is exactly what it has looked like since the Curry variable was removed from Golden State's equation.

To be fair, the absence of a player is an imperfect lens through which to view value for a bunch of contextual reasons, not the least of which is how a team like Golden State is designed to play -- a specific, Curry-centric ecosystem not particularly amenable to abrupt adjustments. These players are not as bad as they have looked without Curry over these last four games.

But by the same token, they aren't close to as good as they looked with Curry, either. I always laugh when my dad calls me saying things like, "This Pat Spencer guy can play!" Everyone looks like they can play next to Curry. And then he goes away and suddenly you're wondering how the hell this guy made the Washington Generals look like one of the best teams in the league. Is he some kind of miracle worker?

It has been revealed that in a basketball sense, that's not far off. Curry's individual production is already virtually unmatched, but it's his exponential powers, his ability to compound the returns of those around him, that set him apart. It's early, yes. Perhaps the Warriors will figure things out the longer Curry is away. Probably not. But maybe they at least can return to competitive functionality. Until then, however, it's pretty hard to not think Curry is the most valuable player in the league when you watch the Warriors play without him.

MLB rumors: Mets' Tarik Skubal follow-up, where Blue Jays turn now, plus Yankees, Phillies, Red Sox, more

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1137 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that the offseason's biggest domino fell late Sunday evening: Tarik Skubal agreed to a nine-year, $450 million contract with the Mets.
  • According to recent reports, it should be a busy week on the hot stove leading up to the expiration of the collective bargaining agreement at 11:59 p.m.
  • Recent findings suggest that the Yankees and left-hander Brent Suter have agreed to a one-year contract worth $4 million, reports the Fresh York Post.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the offseason's biggest domino fell late Sunday evening: Tarik Skubal agreed to a nine-year, $450 million contract with the Mets. It is far and away the richest pitching contract in history, crushing Yoshinobu Yamamoto's $325 million deal with the Dodgers. The Mets still have other things to address, including adding another starter, but they landed the winter's best free agent.

According to recent reports, it should be a busy week on the hot stove leading up to the expiration of the collective bargaining agreement at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1. Here are our top 50 free agents and top 25 trade candidates, and the key offseason dates and deadlines you need to know. Here now are Monday's hot stove happenings.

Recent findings suggest that the Yankees and left-hander Brent Suter have agreed to a one-year contract worth $4 million, reports the Fresh York Post. Suter will make $3.75 million in 2026, and there's a $3.5 million club option for 2027 with a $250,000 buyout. He is the fourth reliever the Yankees have signed this offseason, joining David Bednar (accepted qualifying offer), Tim Hill, and Jonathan Loáisiga.

According to recent reports, with the bullpen mostly assembled, the Yankees figure to pivot to offense the rest of the offseason. They need a third base upgrade over Ryan McMahon and a right-handed hitting catcher to pair with the lefty-swinging Austin Wells. It seems likely the Yankees will go with Anthony Volpe at second base and Spencer Jones in center field, but those positions can be improved as well.

Industry observers note that the Mets have agreed to a deal with free agent first baseman Paul Goldschmidt, reports the New York Post. It's a one-year deal worth $8 million, according to The Athletic. He will presumably pair with Jared Young in a first base platoon. We did not rank Goldschmidt, 39, among our top 50 free agents. He accepted a reduced role for the Yankees over the last two seasons and was a valuable clubhouse presence.

Industry observers note that at this point in his career, Goldschmidt is no longer an everyday player, but he remains a solid platoon bat. He hit .317/.402/.572 against lefties over the last two years, compared to .235/.271/.337 against righties. Goldschmidt can still play a nifty first base as well. The Mets received the worst first base production in the sport in 2027. Even late-career Goldschmidt should be an upgrade.

After missing out on Tarik Skubal, the Blue Jays are now believed to be prioritizing Freddy Peralta, according to MLB Network. Toronto has a very good one-two punch in Dylan Cease and José Soriano. Behind them are Spencer Arrighetti, Cody Ponce (returning from a torn ACL), Trey Yesavage, and maybe Jake Bloss and Ricky Tiedemann. There's room for another starter, for sure.

Peralta, Michael King, and Trevor Rogers are the best available free agent starters now that Skubal has signed. Rogers declined the qualifying offer and is attached to draft pick compensation, which perhaps makes King or Peralta more desirable. Any of the three would boost a Blue Jays rotation that has upside but not much in the way of reliability behind Cease and Soriano.

The Dodgers are not expected to aggressively pursue pitching help after losing out on Tarik Skubal, reports The Athletic. They're comfortable letting things play out and seeing what shakes loose among second- and third-tier free agents. As much as the Dodgers would have liked to retain Skubal, they're in a spot where they didn't absolutely need him.

Industry observers note that despite this year's biceps and knee injuries, Shohei Ohtani is expected to pitch next season. He'll join Tyler Glasnow, Roki Sasaki, Blake Snell, and Yoshinobu Yamamoto in the rotation. Emmet Sheehan, Gavin Stone, and Justin Wrobleski are next in line, with prospects Jackson Ferris and Christian Zazueta not far away. The Dodgers could use another starter but aren't desperate for one.

According to recent reports, the Mariners, Padres, and Phillies are among the teams interested in Red Sox outfielder Jarred Duran, according to MassLive. The Red Sox tendered Duran a contract at Friday's deadline and will now look to trade him. The Jake Bauers signing pushed Duran, who had a .266 on-base percentage in 2026, out of the regular lineup. A trade is the logical next step.

Philadelphia and San Diego badly need outfield help and are obvious fits for Duran. Even if the Mariners manage to re-sign Randy Arozarena, they could use another outfielder, though Duran would be a less-than-stellar fit for a lineup that is already heavily left-handed. Regardless, it seems unlikely Duran will be with the Red Sox by the time Opening Day arrives.

The Blue Jays, Phillies, and Yankees are considered the favorites for Japanese slugger Teruaki Sato, reports MLB.com. The Cubs and Mets are believed to have interest as well. Sato primarily played third base for the Hanshin Tigers but is not regarded as a strong defender, and it is likely that he will play first base or a corner outfield spot in MLB.

It has been revealed that this past season, Sato, 28 in March, hit .306/.383/.609 with 39 home runs and won Japan's Triple Crown. He is similar to Munetaka Murakami in that he has big left-handed power, swing-and-miss concerns, and defensive problems. Murakami is a much more patient hitter, however. Sato is an aggressive swinger and is unlikely to walk much or post a strong on-base percentage.

The Blue Jays offered Tarik Skubal a nine-year contract in the $400 million range before he signed with the Mets, according to The Athletic. Meanwhile, the Dodgers never reached the point of making Skubal an offer, reports ESPN. Los Angeles was known to prefer a short-term, high-dollar contract to a long-term arrangement. Getting Skubal on such a deal always seemed unlikely.

As for the Padres, they put forth an offer in the $400 million range but with deferrals that would have lowered the present day value, reports the Newly introduced York Post. Skubal's contract with the Mets includes $30 million in deferred money, which will lower the present day value some, but not significantly. The exact deferrals in San Diego's offer are unknown.

In a recent development, the Royals and left-handed reliever Caleb Theilbar are in agreement on a one-year deal, per ESPN. Theilbar, 39, was excellent for the Cubs in 2025, but took a step back in 2026, pitching to a 4.86 ERA (87 ERA+) and 1.30 WHIP with 60 strikeouts in 50 innings pitched. He did strand 18 of the 23 runners he inherited, which is an adequate clip for a middle-relief type.

The Royals recently acquired late-inning lefty José Ferrer in a trade and Daniel Lynch remains in the bullpen, so Thielbar could well be their third option as a lefty in relief.

A glimpse of what Tottenham's future might look like came against Crystal Palace on October 31 with Luca Williams-Barnett's thrilling cameo off the bench.

It is a record the club are determined to change. Spurs' renewed strategy has been felt across the Premier League's academy circuit over the past year, with rivals anxious at what lies ahead.

Facilities play a part, too. Spurs' Hotspur Way base, opened in 2012, is renowned as one of the finest training complexes in European football.

The 77-acre state-of-the-art complex in Enfield, which cost £45m to build in 2012 and has since seen significant investment, is home to both the first team and academy, as well as being used regularly by England.

Luka Vuskovic was snapped up before his price tag got too high, and then was sold to Brighton for £50million this summer when he couldn't break into the starting line-up.

Will Lankshear earned Spurs another £20m when he left for Middlesbrough.

With Williams-Barnett already offering a glimpse of what lies ahead, Spurs will hope he is the first of many academy graduates to make the leap.

Recent findings suggest that while four of the 15 grass pitches are reserved exclusively for first-team training, the youngsters benefit from being immersed in the same elite environment as the senior professionals they aspire to emulate. It's an arrangement designed to make the pathway from youth prospect to Premier League footballer feel that little bit closer.

With Williams-Barnett already offering a glimpse of what lies ahead, Spurs will hope he is the first of many academy graduates to make the leap, rather than another reminder of the potential they have previously allowed to slip through their fingers.

For a club that has spent the best part of a decade searching for its next homegrown star, the teenager could yet become the face of a long-overdue academy revival.

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that mikal Bridges was always up against a nearly impossible standard in Upcoming York.
  • Bridges entered Saturday's game against the Trail Blazers averaging 7.5 points per game on putrid 40/30 shooting splits.
  • He's been showing signs of life of late.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that mikal Bridges was always up against a nearly impossible standard in Upcoming York. The Knicks sold everything but their soul to get him. He went from zero to hero over last year's championship run, then right back down to zero to start this season.

Bridges entered Saturday's game against the Trail Blazers averaging 7.5 points per game on putrid 40/30 shooting splits. The familiar chatter was growing louder. Trade him. Or at least bench him. The Knicks entered Saturday having lost Bridges' minutes by a starter-worst five points per 100 possessions this season, per Databallr, and worse, they were +17.8 with him on the bench.

He's been showing signs of life of late. He went for 18 on 8-of-12 shooting against Indiana a week ago. He put up 17 on 7-of-11 in a win over the Raptors on Tuesday. The Knicks entered Saturday having won three straight and seven of their last nine.

Make that four straight and eight of 10 as the Knicks stunned the Blazers 97-96 -- with Bridges turning his ever-extreme dial from zero all the way back up to hero with the shot that just may have turned his season around.

Mike Breen doesn't bring out the double-bang often, but he did it on Saturday when Bridges took an inbound pass at the top of the key and, with the Knicks down two and 3.2 seconds on the clock, dribbled left and pulled up for the second buzzer-beater of his career (both of which have come against the Blazers).

MIKAL BRIDGES HITS THE @TISSOT BUZZER-BEATER AS THE KNICKS WIN THEIR FOURTH STRAIGHT!🚨⏰ Everyone Gets 24 pic.twitter.com/UmtE1mOLRu.

In a recent development, this would've been a gut-punch loss for the Knicks, who were on the verge of fumbling a 23-point halftime lead. Instead, as it turned out, it couldn't have been scripted better. Bridges needed a moment like this.

In a recent development, mike Brown hasn't pulled him from the starting five, but he only played him for 17 minutes in two straight games less than two weeks ago, and Bridges' minutes, largely as a result of that stretch, are down to a career-low 26 a game, which is the same burn Landry Shamet gets. This Nov. 15 portrait of basketball depression just about summed up the state of Bridges' season at that point.

Industry observers note that mikal Bridges and Jose Alvarado on the bench. 😕(h/t @IQfor3) pic.twitter.com/0UU7J4Fd2v.

Fast forward to Saturday night, when Madison Square Garden came alive with more than 50 franchise legends in the building for Homecoming Night, and this is what you call a vibe shift.

KNICKS LEGENDS REACT TO MIKAL BRIDGES' @TISSOT BUZZER-BEATER 🔥 https://t.co/drFU31goFh pic.twitter.com/8HxH5Avnww.

"When, quote-unquote, you think he's struggling, he just keeps playing," Brown remarked of Bridges after Saturday's game. "He doesn't let anything impact him. ... He's not going to get too high, he's not going to get too low. He's been there and done that. So for him to have the ball in his hands at that point in the game, there's a lot of confidence not only coming from him but from his teammates and the staff.".

It has been revealed that in the interest of not totally overreacting to one shot, let's keep some perspective on this. Bridges only had 12 points vs. Portland. The Knicks still lost his 28 minutes by six points, the worst plus-minus of the night. But he made five of his eight shots and established a confident early rhythm.

Bridges certainly hasn't been setting the world on fire, but for the most part he's been looking more like himself after a terrible start. The Knicks are now -49 for the season in Bridges' minutes, but they were -50 over the first three games, meaning he has been a net neutral since. That's nothing to celebrate, but it's not as bad as the prevailing perception.

In a recent development, now look at it the other way. The Knicks are +140 without Bridges on the court this season and, while there's no denying his contribution to that number with too many nothing offensive showings, understand that nearly half of it comes from two games (-24 against the Nets on Nov. 2 and -36 against the Bucks on Nov. 11).

This isn't to suggest Bridges has been anywhere close to good so far. It's just to say that small samples can look like bigger deals than they are, and generally speaking, he's been slowly coming around. Maybe he just needed one game, one shot, one moment to reroute his basketball brain back toward the space he left it in as a playoff hero. Maybe Saturday night was that moment. Like the great Don Henley said: In a Latest York minute, everything can change.

Industry observers note that the Chicago Cubs are signing free-agent left-handed starter Trevor Rogers to a five-year, $120 million contract, ESPN reports. He'll now frontline a Cubs rotation bereft of arms after Matthew Boyd, Shota Imanaga, Kevin Gausman, Clay Holmes and David Peterson all left via free agency this winter. Justin Steele, Cade Horton and Ben Brown, meanwhile, are all working their way back from injuries.

Rogers, who recently turned 29, is coming off a solid campaign for the Baltimore Orioles in 2026:.

Earlier in the offseason, CBS Sports ranked Rogers as the No. 3 overall free agent of the 2026-27 class and the second-ranked starting pitcher behind Tarik Skubal. Here's part of our write-up:.

In a recent development, "Rogers was never able to fully work off the early season stinkers that inflated his ERA, though this is free agency, and ERA is close to the last thing on the minds of interested teams. You're looking forward in free agency, not backward. The underlying performance indicators are very strong, specifically the ability to get chase and avoid the barrel with four pitches (four-seamer, sinker, changeup, sweeper) that light up analytical models. Rogers also has a fifth-pitch cutter and has shown the ability to hammer the strike zone the last two years. There are some lefty Zack Wheeler vibes here. When Wheeler became a free agent after 2019, he already had the analytical stamp of approval, and the belief was he could get to another level with fine-tuning and good health. That is exactly what happened. Lefty Wheeler would obviously be the best-case scenario outcome for Rogers, but the bottom line is he will play the entire 2027 season at age 29, and he throws strikes with four pitches that the pitch data models already consider above average. More than a few teams will undoubtedly see Rogers as a pitcher who is a tweak or two away from finding another gear.".

Rogers took the next step in 2025, and in the 38 starts he's made since the start of that season, he's put up an ERA+ of 128, an FIP of 3.20, and a K/BB ratio of 3.82.

The Orioles made a qualifying offer to Rogers after last season, which means they'll be entitled to a compensatory draft pick now that he's signed elsewhere.

Industry observers note that behind an offense backed by unanimous National League MVP Pete Crow-Armstrong and an elite defense, the Cubs made it to the Wild Card Series before being swept by the Padres, but their pitching, both starting and bullpen, wasn't up to the task. Now, with effectively a blank slate, the Cubs are expected to be in the market for multiple starting pitchers, and Rogers is the first domino.

Rogers' contract is now the third-highest handed out to a Cubs pitcher, behind just Jon Lester (six years and $155 million) and Yu Darvish (six years and $126 million).

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that it is exceedingly rare for teams to have a chance to trade for one of the greatest players in NBA history.
  • It has been revealed that the exception to this, bizarrely, has been Stephen Curry.
  • Sources indicate that there have been various levels of denial involved in all of these rumors, and we'll never really know all the details, but again, it's not as though we hear about this many botched deals for most of Curry's contemporaries.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that it is exceedingly rare for teams to have a chance to trade for one of the greatest players in NBA history. There were never serious rumors, for instance, about LeBron James or Michael Jordan getting traded. Magic Johnson and Kobe Bryant both issued public trade demands, but pulled back before a deal was consummated. Players like this, for the most part, don't make it to the rumor mill because nobody ever thinks they're seriously available.

It has been revealed that the exception to this, bizarrely, has been Stephen Curry. Though the rumors all died once he hit his prime, there is a rich history of teams that nearly traded for the greatest shooter of all time before he became, well, the greatest shooter of all time. At least three notable deals were reportedly scuttled at the finish line:.

Sources indicate that there have been various levels of denial involved in all of these rumors, and we'll never really know all the details, but again, it's not as though we hear about this many botched deals for most of Curry's contemporaries. Of course, Curry differs from those contemporaries in one key way: he was not a sure thing. James came into the NBA as a preordained star. Anyone claiming they knew what Curry was going to become is almost certainly lying. There was quite a bit of doubt about him early in his career, and that doubt informs our latest entry into the Curry trade chronicles.

Dwight Howard appeared on the AM Hoops Show on Saturday and shared something few would be eager to admit: he told his former team, the Orlando Magic, not to trade for Stephen Curry. "I wanted to play with Monta Ellis and the Magic wanted to get Steph. The Magic wanted to get Steph and I said no. I said no because I didn't know. I didn't know Steph Curry was going to be one of the greatest," Howard said, regretfully. Asked specifically if the Magic came to him with this, he confirmed. "At the time, Monta was the one who was playing all the minutes," he added.

In a recent development, howard did not offer a specific trade proposal or window of time when this could have happened, but two options come to mind. The first would be during the 2010-11 season, when Orlando revamped its team in mid-December by making two blockbuster deals that sent Vince Carter, Rashard Lewis, Marcin Gortat and Mickael Pietrus out while bringing back Gilbert Arenas, Hedo Turkoglu, Jason Richardson and Earl Clark. This would make sense as a period of roster transition, and Ellis was the league leader in minutes that season, averaging more than 40 per game across 80 appearances.

In a recent development, but Curry was no slouch that season when it came to availability either. He appeared in 74 games and averaged nearly 34 minutes. His availability didn't become a major concern until a year later, when ankle injuries limited him to just 26 games. At that point, his trade value would have been at its lowest, and Howard's leverage with the team would have been at its height. Howard had a player option for the 2012-13 season that he surprisingly exercised... even though the Magic didn't acquire Ellis. Orlando still wound up trading Howard to the Los Angeles Lakers in the summer of 2012.

Recent findings suggest that on paper, Curry was perhaps the perfect guard to pair with Howard at his peak. Of course, Curry was and remains the perfect player to pair with just about anyone, but Howard, specifically, tried and failed to mesh with two high-usage star guards in Kobe Bryant and James Harden. Curry's eagerness to play off of the ball would have allowed Howard more post-up possessions, a priority of his at the time even if such plays didn't represent great offense. The team could have run through Howard, but still benefitted enormously from the young Curry's presence before eventually shifting in Curry's direction as Howard aged out of his physical prime.

According to recent reports, stan Van Gundy was a pioneer in the 3-point revolution, building a four-out lineup around Howard with players like Lewis and Turkoglu. It's tempting to think about what he could have done with a young Curry, especially since Van Gundy would miss another chance to coach him down the line, when he elected to take the Detroit Pistons job in 2014 rather than continuing to pursue Golden State's vacant position.

Recent findings suggest that but if there ever really was a window for someone to swoop in and steal Curry, it closed after that third, injury-plagued season. Curry broke out in the 2012-13 season by leading the Warriors back to the playoffs, made his first All-Star team a year later, and then a year after that, he won the first of his two MVP awards and four championships. From that point forward, Golden State had no reason to ever entertain the notion of trading Curry, and Howard, like the Suns, Hornets and Bucks, was left to wonder about what might have been.

In a recent development, ironically enough, Howard would get another chance to pair up with Curry in 2013, after Curry had proven himself as Golden State's lead guard. He was a free agent that offseason and met with the Warriors, but seemingly preferred Harden as his running mate, as he signed with the Houston Rockets. The Warriors turned around and used their cap flexibility to add dynasty mainstay Andre Iguodala, an essential part of a team that largely won without high-profile centers like Howard. With the benefit of hindsight, Howard might be one of the most key hidden figures in Golden State's rise to prominence. If he had any inkling of the sort of legend Curry was destined to become, the Warriors dynasty may never have happened.

On Saturday, the Mets locked up center fielder A.J. Ewing to an eight-year extension worth $95 million, with a club option for a ninth year. The 22-year-old Ewing is now signed through 2034.

According to recent reports, there was certainly no urgency on the part of the Mets to lock up Ewing, who would not have become a free agent until after the 2032 season. There might have been urgency on Ewing's part, however. First and foremost, he secured life-changing money after only five months in the big leagues. Second, the collective bargaining agreement will expire at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1, and MLB's various proposals have included not only a salary cap, but also contract limits. The league proposed a maximum five-year contract at 15% of the cap for players who change teams, and six years at 16% of the cap for players who stay with their team.

According to recent reports, ewing's extension may not be possible under the next CBA. That's a pretty good reason to sign a deal now, and it may incentivize other young players to sign long-term extensions between now and the CBA's expiration next week. Here now are 10 players who could get an extension done under the wire this week.

The Brewers aggressively lock up their best young players, including signing Luis Lara and Cooper Pratt to long-term deals even before they made their MLB debuts this summer. Misiorowski, the reigning National League Cy Young winner, could qualify as a Super Two, meaning he would go through arbitration four times rather than the usual three. If nothing else, it would behoove the Brewers to touch base with Misiorowski's representatives and see whether they can find common ground this week.

According to recent reports, because they can afford massive arbitration salaries and avoid the inherent risk that comes with long-term contracts, the Yankees do not give out early career extensions often. In a recent development, although Munetaka Murakami got the attention, Vargas was the White Sox's best player in 2026. Vargas just turned 27 and he's three years away from free agency. Free agent after: 2031 for both.

Victor Wembanyama is hard to put into words. Stephen Curry is the only player I can remember thinking of the same way in the post-Michael Jordan era. Nobody else. With Steph and Wemby, you can't fully describe what you've seen. You try, but in the end you just have to see them to understand. It's totally different than anything you've ever witnessed on a basketball court.

It has been revealed that so here we go again, trying to write about the indescribable Wembanyama, who put 50 points, 19 boards, five blocks and four steals on the Pelicans on Saturday. It feels like we're qualifying one of his "first in history" stat lines about once a week, and indeed, Wembanyama is the first player since blocks and steals became an official stat in 1973 to record those single-game numbers.

Just take a look at this guy making the greatest basketball players in the world look like children.

VICTOR WEMBANYAMA BECOMES THE FIRST PLAYER SINCE 1973-74 TO RECORD 50+ PTS, 15+ REB, 4+ STL AND 5+ BLK IN A GAME!🤯 50 PTS🤯 18 REB🤯 5 BLK🤯 4 STL🤯 5 3PM🤯 32 MINSPURS WIN THEIR 14TH IN 15 GAMES. pic.twitter.com/lPKk3jYNjL.

Industry observers note that before the halftime buzzer had even sounded, Wembanyama had already tallied 32 points, 13 rebounds, three steals and three blocks. That would be a career game for a lot of NBA players. He had played 18 minutes. You can only laugh at this point.

What was even funnier, however, was Wembanyama's comment after the game, when he took a clear stab at, well, whoever he considers his "peers" to be by calling them out for, shall we say, unethical statistical pursuits.

According to recent reports, "It is very special," Wembanyama remarked of reaching the 50-point mark for the second time this season and third time in his career. "But unlike many of my peers, I'm not good at stat-padding. So I haven't reached it as many times as I should have.".

Victor Wembanyama after scoring 50 points: “Unlike many of my peers, I'm not very good at statpadding.” pic.twitter.com/OAogFCa2oi.

So here's what's interesting about this little dig: Wembanyama was definitely guilty of stat-padding his way to 50 in this game. With just more than eight minutes remaining and the Spurs up by 24, Wembanyama could've stayed on the bench after the timeout. The Spurs have made a concerted effort to limit his minutes whenever possible this year. Even in the golden age of comebacks, this game was over.

Sources indicate that but Wemby stayed in and proceeded to take five straight shots on the next five possessions. He was hunting the 50. No question about it. He even admitted as much.

It has been revealed that "The greats of the game, they don't care [about stat-padding]," Wemby said, via The Athletic. "I don't think Wilt [Chamberlain] thought about that when he had 98 points. ... That stepback 3, going right, that I took, it doesn't correlate with this. It didn't fit to the definition [of ethical basketball], for example. So I did try [to stat-pad] at the end.".

Sources indicate that good on Wemby for acknowledging his own hypocrisy, but it raises the question: if you just did the very thing you are railing against, why take the jab in the first place? Every player who has been within range of 50 points has gone for it as long as it's not a competitive game in which quality shots still matter. It's not that major a deal.

But Wemby has done this before. In December of 2025, after the Spurs had just defeated the Thunder, he noted, "I'm just glad to be part of something that's growing to be so beautiful — pure and ethical basketball.".

Recent findings suggest that this was a definite jab at Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's foul-baiting. Wemby, meanwhile, has turned into one of the more theatrical floppers in the league. In almost every way, Wembanyama is different than any other basketball player in the world. But when it comes to this ethical, non-stat-padding basketball soapbox he has climbed upon on numerous occasions, the truth is he's just like everyone else. So enough with the jabs.

  • Earlier in the offseason, CBS Sports ranked Sato, who turns 28 in March, as the No.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Not long after fortifying their rotation with the signing of Trevor Rogers, the Chicago Cubs have struck again by landing slugger Teruaki Soto out of Japan on a six-year, $120 million contract, ESPN reports.

Earlier in the offseason, CBS Sports ranked Sato, who turns 28 in March, as the No. 4 free agent of the current 2026-27 class. Here's part of our write-up:.

"He will play the entire 2027 season at age 28 and is coming off a .306/.383/.609 slash line with 39 home runs, which won him Japan's first Triple Crown since Munetaka Murakami in 2022. Sato has a similar skill set but is not quite Murakami 2.0. He doesn't have quite as much power (but has plenty of it) and won't walk nearly as often, but he does swing and miss a bunch and is unlikely to remain at the hot corner long-term. Sato is a very aggressive hitter who ran a 66% contact rate this past season. That is below the 77% MLB average. The consensus seems to be that he will land at first base or in a corner outfield spot if not next year, then soon. Murakami successfully overcame his contact concerns to slug 35 homers in only 127 games around a hamstring injury. At minimum, that will have MLB teams reconsidering how they evaluate the Japan-to-MLB transition. Like Murakami, Sato carries risk, and like Murakami, his power makes that risk worth the dice roll.".

Sato is expected to play a corner outfield spot for the Cubs even though he's a corner infielder by trade. He does, however, have significant time in the outfield, where the Cubs are in need of help after the incumbent corner outfielders, Ian Happ and Seiya Suzuki, departed in free agency. In 2026, Suzuki and Happ combined for a WAR of 7.8, so the bar for Sato will be relatively high when it comes to replacing a chunk of that value.

It has been revealed that in addition to the $120 million contract owed to Sato, the Cubs also must pay Sato's former team, the Hanshin Tigers, a posting fee. For contracts in excess of $50 million, the posting agreement between MLB and NPB mandates that the posting fee will be 20% of the first $25 million plus 17.5% of the next $25 million plus 15% of the total guaranteed value exceeding $50 million. In the Cubs' case, that comes to a bit more than $20 million they'll owe Hanshin.

The Cubs are coming off a 2026 season in which they won 89 games and earned a postseason berth as the second-place team in the National League Central. In the playoffs, though, they were swept out of the Wild Card Series by the San Diego Padres in two games.

  • Sources indicate that you're expecting me to talk about Wemby's 50-point, 18-rebound, five-block, four-steal performance against the Latest Orleans Pelicans, aren't you?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Let's call the last seven days the NBA's first parity week of the season. Take a look at the standings right now. The No. 2 through the No. 6 seeds in the Eastern Conference standings all have exactly six losses, and while the Philadelphia 76ers hold a three-game lead for the No. 1 seed, they've done so behind a preposterous 12-0 clutch record. When they regress to the mean, we seem destined for an Eastern Conference packed like sardines.

The Western Conference is similarly crunched. The San Antonio Spurs and Los Angeles Lakers sit atop the standings with identical 14-3 records... but seeds 3-9 are all separated by no more than two games. Even the Sacramento Kings got a win this week! The NBA has spent years tinkering in order to create parity, and right now, at least it's getting it. With that unofficial week of parity in the books, let's crown some winners and losers from the last seven days.

Sources indicate that you're expecting me to talk about Wemby's 50-point, 18-rebound, five-block, four-steal performance against the Latest Orleans Pelicans, aren't you? That'd be the easy starting point. We could just as easily kick things off with Luka Dončić's shooting dip, as he has quietly shot roughly 41-31-82 in his past five games, bringing his ridiculous offensive numbers down to slightly more mortal levels and making Wembanyama, for now, the slight MVP betting favorite. Totally reasonable. They're both contributors to his excellent week.

Industry observers note that neither stands up to what Wembanyama did against the Los Angeles Clippers on Thursday. He shunked. That's a word that didn't exist when we woke up on Thursday. It is now, hilariously, a signature moment of Wembanyama's young career. He has apparently dunked so often, so violently that he suffered a hand injury that compelled him to try, and succeed, to shoot a jump shot at the rim.

Recent findings suggest that did Wemby just... shoot it from above the rim??? 🤯😲 pic.twitter.com/1YDxy8mwy8.

The MVP race is for the season. The ridiculous numbers are for the history books. The shunk wins the week. Any time you suffer and overcome a dunking-related injury by inventing a newly introduced form of scoring, you win the week.

In a recent development, the champs have won five in a row and are 11-3 overall since their 0-3 start, but this isn't as simple as the Knicks suddenly looking like the Knicks again. Many of the early season problems are still persisting. Mikal Bridges hit the game-winner on Friday and still shot 3-of-12 on Sunday. Josh Hart missed all four of his 3-pointers on Sunday and is below 26% shooting from deep so far this season. The starters, as a group, are still getting outscored by almost 13 points per 100 possessions after struggling mightily in the past two regular seasons.

Yet they just keep winning. There are obvious basketball reasons for that. Karl-Anthony Towns is getting every rebound, making every shot, and has readopted the playmaking hub role he thrived in throughout the postseason, particularly when it comes to assisting Jalen Brunson. The bench is thriving. Landry Shamet is shooting better than 45% on 3s and Deuce McBride isn't far behind. Tyler Kolek has a 61-to-9 assist-to-turnover ratio.

Recent findings suggest that but there's something deeper here, a resilience and versatility that developed over last season's championship run that is sustaining thus far this season. OG Anunoby has missed the past two games. Towns missed the Blazers game. Bridges and Hart play most of some games and only parts of others because of their early season struggles. Yet Mike Brown just keeps pulling the right levers, and the Knicks just keep figuring it out. Championships can bring about this certainty. The Knicks aren't quite themselves yet, but they have an internalized confidence that came from dominating the playoff crucible a year ago that's paying off handsomely right now.

It's hard to tell what we've seen from the Heat thus far this season that really deserves scrutiny. They started 0-4 in part because opponents weren't missing any 3s. They've gone 8-2 since, but they haven't beaten a single notable, fully healthy opponent during their active seven-game winning streak. No Evan Mobley against the Cleveland Cavaliers. No Jalen Duren against the Detroit Pistons. No Amen Thompson against the Houston Rockets. No... basically anyone against the Oklahoma City Thunder on Sunday, though in fairness, Giannis Antetokounmpo missed that game himself. Miami is something of a Rorschach test so far. You're going to see what you're predisposed to seeing.

Recent findings suggest that but if we're going to panic during the shooting luck-induced losing streak, we're going to have to acknowledge the positives during the winning streak. The maligned Heat offense ranks in the top five over their past 10 games largely because Klay Thompson is shooting like Klay Thompson again and Giannis Antetokounmpo never stopped dunking like Giannis Antetokounmpo. Their core lineups featuring Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo are deterring rim attempts and giving up basically no corner 3s. Andrew Wiggins looks more like Andrew Wiggins since moving to the bench. As tempted as I was to give the third slot to the player development coaches for the Memphis Grizzlies after Cam Spencer's breakout 26-point game against Cleveland, the seven-game Miami winning streak gets the nod.

Industry observers note that the Celtics were too clever by a half with their lineup decisions this weekend. They sat Jayson Tatum and Derrick White against the hapless Kings and then sat Paul George in the second half of that back-to-back against the Stephen Curry-less Golden State Warriors. They lost both very winnable games by a single point when they probably could have ensured a split and maybe even a sweep by aligning the rest. Throw in a 17-point blown lead to the Denver Nuggets and allowing a 40-point fourth quarter against the Orlando Magic and the previously 11-2 Celtics lost all four of their games this week. They're back with the Eastern Conference pack.

It's too early to draw any real conclusions, just as it was too early to crown them Eastern Conference favorites when they were throttling the Sixers two weeks ago, but this week was a reminder of some of the cracks here. Their best player is coming off of a torn Achilles, and their second- and third-best players are in their 30s and have to be managed carefully throughout the season. You can get away with never getting to the basket as a team when you're an elite 3-point shooting outfit. The Celtics haven't been this season, and we're now in Year 2 of Derrick White's 3-point drought (and, for that matter, arguably Year 3 of Jayson Tatum's). Mitchell Robinson will put together a few good stretches and then regress back into the mess he's been for most of the season. Boston has been nearly 22 points stronger per 100 possessions with him off the floor this season.

It has been revealed that the Celtics, given their playing style and roster makeup, are vulnerable to the ebbs and flows of an 82-game season. When everyone's available and they're making their shots, they're going to look unbeatable. This week is what happens when they're not, and considering how frequently that's been the case for them in the playoffs, it's something the Celtics are going to have to learn to play through if they hope to make it through this crowded East.

Industry observers note that slowly but surely, the NBA's cellar dwellers are starting to come around. The Utah Jazz won twice this week. The Chicago Bulls have won three times since Caleb Wilson went down, and they pushed the Denver Nuggets to overtime on Sunday. The Kings got win No. 2 on Saturday, but also pushed the Los Angeles Lakers to the brink on Friday. There is still a whole lot of misery at the bottom of the standings, but all of these teams can find small pockets of optimism.

It has been revealed that not the Bucks, who are now the NBA's last one-win team and owners of a 13-game losing streak. One of those losses came against Miami this week as their former franchise player, Antetokounmpo, throttled them for three quarters before they made the final score look respectable in the fourth quarter. They have the NBA's worst defense comfortably. Beyond a three-game stretch in which second-year guard Kasparas Jakučionis averaged 21 points per game, it's simply been a miserable season in Milwaukee, and it's one that could get worse any day now as the NBA investigates potential salary cap circumvention involving Gary Trent Jr. We all knew the Bucks would struggle with post-Giannis life, but this is worse than anyone could have imagined.

Recent findings suggest that tyrese Haliburton has played four games this season at a roughly All-Star level. The Indiana Pacers are now 3-10 in all other contests, and ESPN reported Friday that Haliburton is set to miss at least another few weeks with a left hamstring strain. This is after a 19-win season played entirely without Haliburton a year ago. At this point, obvious as it sounds, it's simply become clear that the Pacers can't win consistently without their best player. That was obvious in a playoff context, but the regular-season implications here are starting to add up.

In a recent development, indiana is already six games out of a top-six Eastern Conference seed. Even when Haliburton gets back, he's probably not going to be perfectly healthy for the entire rest of the season just given his own history of durability concerns. The East's bottom four teams are thankfully so dreadful that there's probably a floor of No. 11 here, but Indiana will eventually have to pass someone -- presumably the Washington Wizards, perhaps someone else who gets bitten by the injury bug -- just to make it back into the Play-In Tournament picture. Even if they're there, their road to and through the playoffs becomes enormously precarious. It doesn't matter how dangerous you are in a playoff setting if you can't actually survive the regular season and make it there. It's too early to say that's where Indiana is headed, but the danger is very real.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If there is any truth to the adage that the NFL season does not truly start until Thanksgiving, then now is the time to start taking the playoff race seriously. As the calendar turns to Week 12 and a loaded holiday slate, all seven seeds in both conferences are up for grabs, and there are a number of teams beyond the current cut line that could not only make their way into the bracket but also compete for home-field advantage in the postseason.

Anyone that aims to lock up a first-round bye in the NFC has to get through the San Francisco 49ers, which is a daunting task considering how dominant they appeared on the Week 11 edition of "Sunday Night Football.".

According to recent reports, and in the AFC, the Jacksonville Jaguars learned a difficult lesson on Sunday about how slim the margins are in the race for the No. 1 seed when they suffered a costly setback against the Newly introduced York Giants.

With seven weeks of regular-season action to go, here is a snapshot of the playoff picture in both NFL conferences.

According to recent reports, remaining schedule: vs. Chiefs, at Patriots, at Packers, vs. Bears, at Broncos, at Dolphins, vs. Jets.

The only blemish on the Bills' resume is a three-point divisional loss to the Patriots, but that should not come back to bite them in the AFC East race as they hold a commanding four-game lead. It does make them vulnerable in the battle for the conference's No. 1 seed, though. The schedule is about to stiffen up following a four-game stretch in which Josh Allen feasted on beleaguered opponents and the defense corrected its early-season woes by allowing no more than 12 points in any of those contests.

It has been revealed that remaining schedule: at Steelers, vs. Dolphins, at Jets, at Raiders, vs. Bills, at Patriots, vs. Chargers.

That the Broncos fended off Fernando Mendoza and the Raiders was critical for Denver's chances of winning the AFC West. Sean Payton's squad holds a tiebreaker over the Chiefs thanks to their higher win percentage against common opponents. It was a rare win by double digits for a team that is prolific at squeaking out victories by a one-score margin and increased the win streak to six games, which is tied for the longest in the conference.

According to recent reports, remaining schedule: vs. Titans, at Bears, vs. Steelers, at Texans, at Cowboys, vs. Commanders, at Colts.

According to recent reports, trevor Lawrence endured uncharacteristic struggles in a loss to the Giants that halted the Jaguars' momentum. In each of their previous four games, they scored at least 31 points. They managed only 18 against Upcoming York. The AFC South is still theirs by a three-game margin, so the defeat only has implications for seeding inside the top four. This team went all-in at the trade deadline and would thus figure to be disappointed with anything less than the No. 1 seed, but so long as everything comes together in the postseason, one loss in Week 11 will not haunt them.

In a recent development, remaining schedule: vs. Saints, at Browns, vs. Chiefs, at Panthers, at Colts, vs. Ravens, vs. Browns.

In a recent development, monday's last-second loss to the Commanders did not drop the Bengals out of first place in the AFC North, but they slipped behind the Jaguars on a tiebreaker after their head-to-head defeat earlier in the season. Cincinnati is fortunate that none of the other teams in its division picked up a win in Week 11.

Sources indicate that remaining schedule: at Bills, at Rams, at Bengals, vs. Patriots, vs. 49ers, at Chargers, vs. Raiders.

It has been revealed that the battle with the Broncos to secure home-field advantage in the Wild Card round could come down to the last week of the season. The Chiefs have done nearly everything they can to lock up one of those prized seeds yet find themselves on the outside looking in due to Denver's tiebreaker in the division. Kansas City has been mauling overmatched opponents of late and needs that to translate to the much stiffer competition that lies ahead over the next five weeks.

It has been revealed that remaining schedule: vs. Raiders, vs. Bengals, vs. Falcons, at Giants, at Ravens, vs. Colts, at Bengals.

The Browns hold a tiebreaker over the Steelers for the No. 6 seed because of their divisional win percentage. They split the regular-season series with Pittsburgh and won their only other AFC North contest, 13-10, over the Baltimore Ravens. Among the more pleasant surprises of the entire NFL season is what first-year coach Todd Monken continues to achieve in turning Deshaun Watson back into a serviceable starting quarterback and how defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg constructed a competitive group following the offseason Myles Garrett trade.

It has been revealed that remaining schedule: vs. Broncos, vs. Texans, at Jaguars, vs. Ravens, vs. Panthers, at Titans, at Ravens.

Industry observers note that it was only three weeks ago that the Steelers held sole possession of the AFC North lead. Everything since then has been a disaster. They no-demonstrated a week ago in a primetime loss to the Bengals and, on Sunday, were on the wrong side of the Eagles, who snapped a seven-game losing streak. That in-state loss marked a new low for the 2026 Steelers. They remain on the right side of the postseason cut line, but it is a tenuous position.

It has been revealed that no team outside the top seven is better than 5-5, and that lone .500 team will be without its quarterback until further notice. The Patriots (5-5) would be the top contender to move up the ladder if Drake Maye were healthy, but in his absence, the door is open for teams a little further down. That includes the Texans (4-6), who could become just the second team in NFL history to start a season 0-4 and reach the playoffs. The pickings are slim behind them, as the Ravens (4-7) and Raiders (4-7) are operating with a backup quarterback and rookie signal-caller, respectively.

Remaining schedule: vs. Seahawks, at Giants, vs. Rams, at Chargers, at Chiefs, vs. Eagles, at Cardinals.

In a recent development, if a decisive win over a fellow championship contender and a 35-point outburst against the NFL's top defense does not cement the 49ers as Super Bowl favorites, then nothing will. San Francisco is undoubtedly the team to beat. Mike Evans' return in the Mexico City Game injected even more life into the offense and gives Kyle Shanahan yet another weapon to deploy in the weeks to come as he unleashes an unstoppable attack on the rest of the league. The NFC is the 49ers' to lose.

Remaining schedule: vs. Bears, at Falcons, vs. Titans, at Vikings, vs. Giants, at Bears, at Packers.

Sources indicate that the Lions hold a tiebreaker over the Bears for the NFC North lead with the greater win percentage in division games, but that will not matter in just a few days when the head-to-head result between the two on Thanksgiving determines who has the inside track to home-field advantage in the Wild Card round. Detroit, as it stands, is the top threat to the 49ers at the top of the conference and owns the kind of offensive star power it would take to unseat them from the NFC's catbird seat should they square off in the postseason.

It has been revealed that remaining schedule: at Colts, vs. 49ers, at Seahawks, vs. Browns, at Lions, at Cowboys, vs. Eagles.

The Giants passed their biggest test of the year on Sunday when they took down the Jaguars in a colossal 23-18 victory. Every other win on their ledger is against a sub-.500 team, so the Week 11 triumph was by far the most impressive and legitimized their division lead. They remain the only NFC East team with a winning record and own a defense that seems capable of keeping them in control of their own destiny in the hunt for a top-four playoff seed.

It has been revealed that remaining schedule: at Buccaneers, at Vikings, vs. Saints, vs. Bengals, at Steelers, vs. Seahawks, vs. Falcons.

Such is the state of the NFC South that the Panthers are merely .500 yet own a two-game lead over the rest of the division. Every other team is 3-7. There exists a realistic path for Carolina to move up to the No. 3 seed since the NFC East is nearly as weak as their own division, but that is probably the ceiling. Back-to-back wins and Chuba Hubbard's emergence as a prominent bell-cow running back have the Panthers trending the right way.

According to recent reports, remaining schedule: at Lions, vs. Jaguars, at Dolphins, at Bills, vs. Packers, at Lions, at Vikings.

The Jeffery Simmons effect is obvious. The Bears are unbeaten since they traded for the superstar defensive tackle, and he came through with three sacks on Sunday to match a career high and aid Chicago in defeating the Saints, 21-13. Simmons' presence will be of the utmost importance next week against the Lions' incredible rushing attack and the following week when the Bears take on Jacksonville in an intra-conference blockbuster.

Remaining schedule: vs. Falcons, vs. Panthers, at Patriots, vs. Lions, vs. Commanders, at Jets, vs. Bears.

Is it time to be concerned about the Vikings? All of a sudden, Minnesota has lost three of its last four games. Sure, the "Sunday Night Football" disaster can be chalked up to playing against a stellar offense in a not-even-remotely-neutral environment in Mexico City. But the Vikings are going to have to beat teams of the 49ers' caliber to get to the mountaintop, and they have done nothing but lose to them over the last month. The elite defense will only take them so far, and on days like Sunday when not even that group shows up, things can get really bleak.

Industry observers note that remaining schedule: at Rams, at Saints, vs. Bills, vs. Dolphins, at Bears, vs. Texans, vs. Lions.

According to recent reports, the NFC North is what most expected the NFC West to be in that it could send three or four teams to the postseason. There is a battle between the two divisions for the final wild card spot. The Seahawks and Rams are both 6-4, so Seattle holds the tiebreaker based on win percentage in division games. But the Packers then hold a tiebreaker over Seattle due to their conference win percentage.

Recent findings suggest that the NFC North and NFC West will cannibalize themselves to an extent, which may open the door for the Cowboys (5-6) or even the Commanders (4-5-1) to sneak their way into the No. 7 seed. But there is a chasm between them and the teams ahead of them in terms of overall team quality. The Seahawks (6-4) and Rams (6-4) are both more complete squads. There might only be room for one of them to get into the bracket, though, which would be a surprise given the former's status as the reigning champion and the latter's preseason outlook as the Super Bowl favorite.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • While thinking over the last few days about his first press conference as Manchester United boss, Mauricio Pochettino would not have expected drones and the latest Grand Theft Auto video game to be top of the agenda.
  • Having touched down in Manchester on Wednesday, taking a private jet laid on by United in the immediate aftermath of the United States’ game in Cincinnati against Haiti, it has been a whirlwind 48 hours for Pochettino and his staff.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 07:00 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 07:10 EST, 20 November 2026.

While thinking over the last few days about his first press conference as Manchester United boss, Mauricio Pochettino would not have expected drones and the latest Grand Theft Auto video game to be top of the agenda.

Having touched down in Manchester on Wednesday, taking a private jet laid on by United in the immediate aftermath of the United States’ game in Cincinnati against Haiti, it has been a whirlwind 48 hours for Pochettino and his staff.

On Thursday, he took charge of training for the first time against the backdrop of question marks around Bryan Mbeumo’s decision to post late into the night about popular new video game GTA VI.

By the time the day ended, the concern at hand was far more pressing as a drone pilot filmed and uploaded to YouTube a 12-minute video from Pochettino’s first session at Carrington.

How worried Pochettino actually is about the footage – which has since been pulled from YouTube, with a grovelling apology issued – remains to be seen but only this summer did the Argentine concede that ‘we are in an era of spies’.

The footage wasn’t a tactical golden ticket for Liverpool, but what was there to take from it?

A drone pilot filmed and uploaded to YouTube a 12-minute video from Mauricio Pochettino’s first training session as Manchester United manager.

The players get to work, with United's coaching staff seemingly unaware that their every move is being followed from the skies.

Pochettino sides have had a consistent set-up with and without the ball over the years.

The Argentine and his staff have, more often than not, leaned into a back-three in possession, shifting to a back-four without the ball.

In the drone footage we could see the United squad divided into three groups with one XI out on a different training pitch with Pochettino and coach Toni Jimenez.

That group were lined up in what appeared to be that preferred in-possession set-up, with academy defender Reece Munro tucking in from right back to form a back-three alongside Harry Maguire and Ayden Heaven, traditional centre backs in a back-four.

Pochettino likes to have at least one full back push on extremely high to provide the width and in this snippet of his first training session, that responsibility landed on the shoulders of teenager Harry Amass, who has struggled for minutes this season, getting a total of just 29 under Michael Carrick.

The United players are put into position by Pochettino at Carrington.

Similarly, Pochettino has often shown a desire to play No 10s – or attacking midfielders – quite narrow. And that is what we saw here, with Amass and Mbeumo providing the width. Mbeumo was on the right of a 4-2-3-1 shape with Matheus Cunha and 17-year-old academy talent Jaume Camacho playing narrower and Joshua Zirkzee up front.

The formation becomes a 3-2-4-1 in possession with the full back pushing on to the wing, creating two No 10s behind the lone striker.

The footage was significant in that it revealed Pochettino is implementing his ideas from day one and is wasting no time in trying to embed a style he needs players to get up to speed with quickly.

But little should be read into the personnel given it was an amalgamation of young players and senior regulars.

We could see academy players Amass, Camacho and Munro among the 10 outfield players, along with Cunha, Heaven, Maguire, Kobbie Mainoo, Mbeumo, Andrey Santos and Zirkzee.

Of the 10 that were put to task by Pochettino, only four have started more than five league games this season.

It is highly improbable that the personnel used will be anywhere close to the starting XI at Anfield on Sunday.

The footage also indicated games of one-touch rondos going on between the two other groups which were divided between the rest of Pochettino’s coaching team, which includes his son Sebastiano and Miguel D’Agostino, as well as trusted assistant Jesus Perez.

Pochettino greets his latest players including Bryan Mbeumo, who lined up out wide in the first training session.

United's players start a 'rondo', where one defender stands in the middle and tries to pinch the ball from the players stood around the edge - who are allowed one touch at a time.

One group included Diogo Dalot, Leny Yoro, Lisandro Martinez, Matthijs de Ligt, Youri Tielemans, Mason Mount and Noussair Mazraoui. The other was academy-led with Bruno Fernandes leading a rondo that featured Shea Lacey, Jack and Tyler Fletcher, Dan Armer, as well as Jaydan Kamason.

But the use of Mbeumo in Pochettino’s work was one of the most interesting aspects, largely because he was back operating in a wider role.

Sources indicate that with injuries hampering Benjamin Sesko, Mbeumo has had to spend a lot of the season deployed through the middle. That could well have to continue given Sesko is not anticipated to return until late January, but Pochettino’s decision to use Zirkzee as the figurehead in his set-up was intriguing.

It has been revealed that pochettino’s principles and set-up won’t vary too much; the onus now is on players to adapt. But Pochettino and Jimenez did look to have players in the correct positions. There were no obvious experiments – which makes sense when time is of the essence.

Amass plays off the left, Munro is a centre back, Maguire is comfortable in the middle of any back three, Camacho plays as a No 10 in the academy, both Mainoo and Santos have played together in a double pivot at the base of midfield and Zirkzee is a centre forward.

Pochettino likes a centre forward who can drop in to allow No 10s to run beyond and that suits Zirkzee’s style well, allowing him to be involved as a link man and not isolated with his back to goal.

Mbeumo works better running in behind as a counter-attacking striker, playing on the shoulder of the last defender.

How Pochettino uses Mbeumo over the longer term remains curious because swap out Camacho for Fernandes and Amass for Dorgu and there is a plausible set-up for success, with Mbeumo holding width on the right, Cunha and Fernandes in those central pockets they crave most, and Dorgu holding width off the left.

Lisandro Martinez (left) and Leny Yoro also meet Pochettino and his staff at Carrington.

Pochettino’s track record of working with and improving young players became immediately apparent, with so many given an introduction to his staff and their methods on day one.

While both Jack and Tyler Fletcher, along with Amass, Lacey and Bendito Mantato have made their first-team debuts, it was a golden opportunity in particular for Camacho, the stand-out player in the academy this season following the exit of JJ Gabriel.

United routinely promote multiple academy players each day to bolster numbers in first-team training sessions and it’s a good way for staff to bridge the gap in speed, physicality and intensity between senior and youth football.

Every manager that comes in likes to take on a project and when Ruben Amorim walked through the door it was Godwill Kukonki that caught the eye of staff.

Gabriel became a training mainstay in the months prior to his bombshell request to terminate his contract, and now Camacho, Munro and Armer are working towards first-team debuts instead.
