💡 Key Takeaways
  • When I think about Thanksgiving, I think about going to my grandparents' house growing up.
  • Around midnight — sometimes later — we'd arrive at my grandparents' doorstep, weary but happy.
  • And then there was Thanksgiving Day, which meant football.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When I think about Thanksgiving, I think about going to my grandparents' house growing up. We'd leave immediately after my dad got off work on Wednesday and drive from my hometown in rural Virginia to my mom's parents in Latest Jersey. A quick stop at the McDonald's was the only time we'd leave our route. We'd drive extra miles to avoid traffic. I'd try, often unsuccessfully, to fight off sleep on the drive up.

Around midnight — sometimes later — we'd arrive at my grandparents' doorstep, weary but happy. They'd always greet us with smiling faces, no matter the hour.

And then there was Thanksgiving Day, which meant football. My grandpa, a die-hard Giants fan, would lead our collective yelling at the TV, hoping the Cowboys would lose, and we'd pity-root for the Lions, who seemingly never won.

According to recent reports, the results fade, but what I remember is my family being together. It wasn't perfect. It got harder as my grandparents got older. We'd laugh, we'd cheer, we'd wish it could last forever.

Industry observers note that it's been several years since then, but I still remember my grandparents waving us goodbye, my grandpa good-heartedly reminding my dad to go south, not north, on the turnpike. It felt like just minutes earlier, they had been standing in that doorway welcoming us in. It always went too fast.

According to recent reports, so ahead of our six lessons, let me give you a non-football one: Try to cherish this week. If you can do it with family, great. If you can do it with friends, great. If all you can do is call or text, great. It doesn't have to be perfect. Whether you watch every football game this week or none at all, I hope you're surrounded by people you love.

Sources indicate that coach of the Year has become so misconstrued, and not just in the NFL. Every individual player award honors the best player, but for some reason Coach of the Year honors the coach whose team exceeds expectations most.

So, once again, Kyle Shanahan's magnificent job will likely go unrewarded, simply because he's done too good a job for too long. An early congratulations to either John Harbaugh or Todd Monken for winning. They've done magnificent jobs.

In a recent development, but Kyle Shanahan is the best coach in the NFL this season. The 49ers just dismantled the Vikings to move to 9-1. They have won games in Australia and Mexico and Seattle and Dallas, all places with their own unique challenges. They have won games using wide receivers they never imagined having to count on.

Recent findings suggest that thought you saw the best of Brock Purdy? Think again. I've written at length about why Purdy deserves MVP and is much more than just a product of the Shanahan system, but there's no doubt Shanahan has raised his game immensely. This offense is so well-constructed, so prepared for each and every task each and every week and so connected.

The Vikings love to blitz. Purdy shredded them with quick passes: 12-for-13 for 161 yards and two touchdowns on throws released in 2.5 seconds or faster. Minnesota entered the night leading the NFL in sack rate and pressure rate. It managed just one sack and a 29% pressure rate, both season lows.

This is nothing new, by the way.

Oh yeah, and Shanahan also made the excellent hire of defensive coordinator Raheem Morris, who has helped turn this defense from quite poor to elite.

It has been revealed that it's silly that we'll look back and likely see someone else win Coach of the Year. Shanahan has never won the award, by the way, even though he's been the best or among the best in the profession for nearly a decade. Andy Reid, who's fourth all-time in wins, has won it once, back in 2002 with the Eagles. Sean McVay has won it once since becoming a head coach in 2017. Kevin Stefanski, a perfectly solid coach but nothing more, has won it twice.

In a recent development, again, even if he doesn't win "Coach of the Year," Shanahan is very much the defining coach of this year. He'd gladly take a Lombardi Trophy over any individual award, anyway.

According to recent reports, one day after Brian Flores' normally excellent defense was shredded, one of his disciplines had his best performance yet. Commanders defensive coordinator Daronte Jones and his unit were terrific in a 22-20 upset win over the Bengals.

Sources indicate that jones, like Flores, brings extra pressure, major time. Washington is third in blitz rate this year. Joe Burrow has destroyed blitzes all year, but on Monday night, not so much.

Jones was without his best cornerback, Amik Robertson, but refused to back down. His corners played physically, aggressively and well. The safeties followed in kind. And while Cincinnati's running game has never been a strength, Washington turned it into a decided weakness. The Bengals' 14% rushing success rate was the worst by any team in any game this year.

It has been revealed that jones has this defense moving in the right direction, too. In November, the Commanders rank 15th in defensive EPA per play; they were 23rd before that. They've done a good job stopping the run and limiting explosives, largely because they have the third-lowest missed tackle rate in the league. Washington hasn't allowed more than 23 points in a game since Week 5.

There will be massive-picture coaching questions in Washington if the team doesn't make the playoffs, but Jones has done solid work under the radar.

I wrote about this in our Week 11 overreactions, but the Steelers are once again a team with a winning record and little chance of winning a playoff game. Here, though, let's talk about the style.

Aaron Rodgers is now completing 21.6% of his passes thrown 20+ yards downfield. While he is throwing way more of them this year — only Jordan Love has more than Rodgers' 51 attempts — they're mostly performative "See? I'll still take shots downfield" throws that are low-percentage floaters. Only Cam Ward and recently released Daniel Jones have a lower completion rate on these throws.

It has been revealed that the run game can be quite good. In fact, the Steelers are second in rushing EPA per play this year at 0.06. Earlier in the season, it seemed they finally had one truly sterling offensive aspect. This made them different.

But when the run game isn't going well, as has been the case the last two weeks, Pittsburgh has nothing else. The Steelers are 4-0 when their EPA per rush is above their overall season mark and 2-4 when it is below it. Pittsburgh was at -0.19, second-worst of the season, in the Week 11 loss to the Eagles.

The Steelers have been the same as they've been during this playoff win drought: poor quarterbacking, good-not-great defense.

It has been revealed that K. Pickett, M. Rudolph, M. Trubisky.

Just a dull, stuck-going-nowhere team archetype and a franchise that seems fine with it.

Recent findings suggest that the Chiefs' three-game winning streak has coincided with a soft schedule. There's not a ton to take away from it in terms of Kansas City's standing in the championship-contending pecking order.

But on an individual level, Emmett Johnson is a beast. In his two starts with Kenneth Walker III out, Johnson has 134 yards from scrimmage and three touchdowns.

Emmett Johnson has now recorded back to back 100 yard rushing games since taking over for Kenneth Walker.23 CAR, 105 RUSH YDS, 1 TD, 4 REC, 38 REC YDS vs Cardinals.Johnson's OROY chances have skyrocketed over the last two weeks. https://t.co/dt5FdKVwLi pic.twitter.com/tNep8zsuxb.

Recent findings suggest that johnson currently leads all running backs in 7.0 yards per touch (min. 50 touches). He also leads all running backs in tackle avoidance rate (36.8), which is also first and slightly higher than tackle-avoiding machine Walker III.

It has been revealed that johnson has a true three-down skill set. Only 11.3% of his rushes go for 0 or negative yards, the fourth-lowest rate among all running backs with at least 50 touches, and he has turned several potential losses into gains.

Walker is a stud. He'll be the feature back when he returns from his groin injury. But Johnson has proved he not only deserves a legit complementary role down the stretch and beyond, but with his pass-catching acumen, he can actually be a weapon, too.

The Colts got thumped 26-3 by the Texans on Thursday, and that somehow wasn't the worst aspect of their week. Not even close.

According to recent reports, one day after that, Indianapolis released Daniel Jones, and shortly after that, reports surfaced that at the trade deadline, the Colts had turned down the Ravens' offer of a fourth-and fifth-round pick for Jones (the fifth would be returned if Baltimore made the playoffs). Now, they get nothing for Jones and will carry a $35.2 million dead cap hit in 2027.

Recent findings suggest that if interim GM Ed Dodds wasn't already filling in for a fired GM (Chris Ballard), this would be a fireable offense. Maybe it is, anyway. The Colts sold away many of their franchise pillars but stopped at Daniel Jones?

According to various reports, the Colts turned away multiple suitors for Jones, including Baltimore's potentially lucrative one; multiple suitors for Jonathan Taylor, who fetched offers for a second-round pick plus more; at least one offer that included a fourth-round pick for veteran defensive tackle Grover Stewart, who's 33 and in a contract year.

I gave the Colts a D+ in my trade deadline grades and, upon first reflection, thought I might have been a little harsh. Indianapolis did get decent draft capital back for the moves it did make. But now, I think that mark might be generous. Every meaningless hard hit Taylor takes, and every meaningless double-team Stewart takes on, is just that. Meaningless.

Industry observers note that the Colts have very little young, cost-controlled talent. They don't have their first-round pick in 2027. They will have a fresh GM and, likely, a new coach. They are arguably the worst team in the NFL in 2026. They will be in the running for worst team in the NFL in 2027 and potentially 2028. They just turned down draft capital for a player they didn't even want. If there were a class in mismanaging an enterprise worth billions of dollars, the Colts' front office could do a great job teaching it.

According to recent reports, if it feels like there's been a little bit of a midseason lull, it's because there has been. In November, there's been a ton of blowouts — seven games decided by 15+ every week from Week 8-10, and then a lot of byes and semi-competitive games in Week 11.

But the league is cranking it up a notch this coming week.

In a recent development, the Bears have won five straight, but their last two are over the lowly Buccaneers and Saints, with a bye in between. The Lions have won six straight, but the last three are over the Dolphins, the Patriots (mostly without Drake Maye) and the Buccaneers. I'm a huge believer in "you can only beat who's on your schedule." But in terms of learning about these teams, the past few weeks haven't been very helpful.

Recent findings suggest that that all changes this week. On Thanksgiving, the 8-2 Lions host the 8-2 Bears (on CBS and streaming on Paramount+, by the way!), which should be an absolute banger.

This is far from the only example. Get your nap in early, because later that night, Chiefs at Bills is a can't-miss. Buffalo has seemed almost bored — and certainly hasn't been very sharp — in wins over the Ravens, Carson Wentz-led Vikings, Jets and Dolphins. But they'll absolutely be locked in against their bitter rival. The Chiefs, meanwhile, have cruised past the Jets, Falcons and Saints after a tough loss to the Broncos. We have questions about Josh Allen's turnovers, Patrick Mahomes' deep-passing renaissance — is it real or fake? — and much more.

Unai Emery is building Aston Villa 2.0 and this was a night when his newly introduced kids on the block produced clear signs of lift-off for the next chapter.

Emery always springs into life on European nights and his reconstructed team secured their first win and goals of the season to leave Villa’s 1,700 fans singing in the rain.

Ten summer signings have arrived during a summer of upheaval, which included plenty of high-profile departures after the club’s Europa League triumph in May.

Yet this was an evening that will have further energised Emery on his return to the Champions League.

Only five of that starting XI from the second leg of the quarter-final remain and one of them, midfielder Amadou Onana, is out until next year after sustaining a serious knee injury at the World Cup with Belgium.

With European heavyweights Barcelona, PSG and Borussia Dortmund to come in the league phase, this always felt like a game Villa probably needed to win.

Aston Villa are back in the Champions League and in familiar territory with an unfamiliar team.

This will be their third match at the Jan BreydelStadion in less than two years but much has changed with the players that last competed here for Unai Emery.

Two of the goalscorers in the club’s last outing in Bruges were Leon Bailey and Marco Asensio, who are no longer at the club.

Of course, they are not the only players that have left and this is a upcoming-look Emery team hoping for lift-off this season.

Villa are the Europa League winners but this could be a tricky evening against the Belgian Pro League champions.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of Aston Villa’s Champions League opener against Club Brugge. Unai Emery’s side voyage across the Channel to face the Belgian champions having triumphed in last season’s Europa League and finished fourth in the Premier League. The Villa mothership has since sailed into choppy waters, though, with a raft of substantial-name sales preceding a run of two defeats and a draw in the league. An opening-weekend thrashing by Brighton and Hove Albion proved quite the storm for Emery’s fresh-look crew.

Sources indicate that morgan Rogers alighted for Chelsea in a deal worth £117m, a record fee for an English player, and goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez followed soon after, while Youri Tielemans moved to Manchester United. Ezri Konsa and Ollie Watkins completed the exodus of leading men with late-August moves to Arsenal and Al-Hilal respectively. To remedy the outgoings, Villa twice broke their transfer record this summer, pipping Newcastle United to the signing of Johan Manzambi (£59.5m) before landing Nicolas Jackson (£65m, including add-ons), and added Taylor Harwood-Bellis and Ibrahim Mbaye on deadline day. Whether they can hit the ground running remains to be seen, but Emery has a task on his hands aligning his upcoming recruits before the scrutiny intensifies.

Although Villa swept aside Brugge 6-1 across two legs in the Champions League quarter-finals two seasons ago, here Blauw-Zwart (Blue-Black) represent a stern test having made the Jan Breydel Stadium a fortress in last year’s tournament. Their only home defeat in the league phase came against Arsenal, with a 3-3 draw against Barcelona backed up by 4-1 and 3-0 victories over Monaco and Marseille respectively. Belgium’s second-most decorated club have won seven of the last 11 league titles and know how to win matches. In Yann Sommer, Ivan Leko has one of world football’s most experienced goalkeepers, who kept the most clean sheets in the 2024-25 edition of the Champions League (seven). Captain Hans Vanakan, Brandon Mechele and Joaquin Seys were part of Rudi Garcia’s Belgium World Cup squad, and German striker Nicolò Tresoldi already has four goals in six matches this term. English midfielder Freddie Potts could also feature, having settled in nicely in West Flanders having moved from West Ham United during the summer.

The earlier 5.45pm kick-off time, means Villa, Brugge, LASK and AEK Athens have the opportunity to top the 36-team league …at least for a couple of hours.

Actually, that's a lie. I have no recipes. I've never cooked a turkey in my life, and I don't even know how my oven works. I only have one favorite side dish (sweet potatoes), and my favorite dessert is fermented grapes, which I think most normal people refer to as wine. I also like pumpkin pie. As a matter of fact, when it comes to Thanksgiving, I will eat anything in pie form.

Alright, let's get to the picks, because if we don't do it now, there's a chance I might not stop talking about food, and if that happens, I'll probably get hungry, and I don't like to write when I'm hungry.

Alright, let's get to the Thanksgiving edition of the picks.

That is not a typo; there's a game on Wednesday this week, but please do not remind Kelly Stafford about that because she seems kind of mad at the NFL right now for stealing the Rams' bye week.

Kelly Stafford recently called out the NFL for making the Rams the only team without a true bye week this season.With injuries piling up, does LA have a legitimate reason to be frustrated with the scheduling?#Rams #RamsHouse #KellyStafford #MatthewStafford #NFL pic.twitter.com/lVsHAr9ZGM.

The Rams and Packers both got a bye in Week 11, but they didn't really get a bye because they were preparing for this game.

The NFL has spent the past few years trying to squeeze a game into every possible viewing window, and that's how we ended up with a game on Thanksgiving Eve for the first time in league history. The NFL is trying to turn Thanksgiving Eve into a national holiday, but if they had done their homework, they would've known that it's already a national holiday: It's Drinksgiving (or something like that).

It has been revealed that there's a reason the night before Thanksgiving is the biggest bar night of the year. Everyone goes home for Thanksgiving, and they have nothing to do on Wednesday night, so they all go to the bar. If you're over 21, raise your hand if you've ever been to a bar on the night before Thanksgiving. OK, so that's all of us.

I'm not sure what the record is for the most people watching a game at a bar, but this is going to break it. If this game gets 15 million viewers, I imagine it will be 142 people watching at home and 14,949,858 people watching at a bar. And probably about 50,000 others who are actually trying to watch a random movie on Netflix but accidentally turn the game on (Yup, this game is on Netflix).

I went on that long rant about bars because I needed some extra time to figure out who I'm going to pick in this game. (At this point, I should probably just make my pick from a bar.) On one hand, the Rams will have Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald on the field for just the third time this season. They're going up against a Packers team that can't run the ball — we're going to take a brief pause here so we can truly appreciate how bad the Packers have been at running the ball this year.

Industry observers note that will the Packers be able to run the ball against the Rams on Thanksgiving Eve? Well... pic.twitter.com/QSiLUN0VgC.

If the Packers can't run, that means Jordan Love is going to have to throw the ball 50 times, and you do not want to be stuck in a situation where you have to throw the ball 50 times with guys like Garrett and Donald breathing down your neck. Advantage: Rams.

Industry observers note that on the flip side, the Rams' offense could have some trouble in this game. That's mainly because I have no idea who Matthew Stafford is going to throw the ball to. With Puka Nacua and Davante Adams both out, I now understand why Kelly Stafford wanted an entire bye week: It was probably so her husband would have some time to find someone else to throw the ball to. Of course, the Rams could just decide to not throw the ball at all, which actually might work, because they rank seventh overall in rushing yards per game this year.

Industry observers note that with Blake Corum and Kyren Williams leading the way, the Rams have had a sneaky good rushing attack this season. It's gotten hot over the past four weeks, with the Rams averaging 163.5 yards per game on the ground in that span.

Sources indicate that the Packers are 1-4 this season when their opponent rushes for at least 100 yards, and their only win came by three points over a team (Buccaneers) that was starting an undrafted quarterback (Jalon Daniels), so I'm not even going to count that. Green Bay will get Micah Parsons back in this game, but I'm not sure how effective he'll be after not playing in a single game for 11 months.

The Rams are celebrating Thanksgiving with a full Thanksgiving menu at their concession, and I feel like they're also going to be celebrating a win.

Sources indicate that the Rams will have a special Thanksgiving menu at SoFi on Wednesday:-Smoked Turkey Legs with cranberry barbecue sauce.-Turkey Pot Pie with fall vegetables and herb béchamel in a puff pastry.-Smoked Turkey with mashed potatoes & gravy, herb dressing and cranberry sauce. pic.twitter.com/49lusNrGtn.

And it's a good to see hey have some specialty drinks in there. Even the Rams are celebrating the biggest bar night of the year.

Thursday, 1 p.m. ET (CBS, Stream: Paramount+).

Industry observers note that I'm not going to tell you how to strategy your Thanksgiving, but if you need some help mapping out your day around the three games on the schedule, that's why I'm here. For one, the NFL has decided to throw your entire schedule off by 30 minutes this year with the Lions' game kicking off at 1 p.m. ET. The early game used to start at 12:30 p.m. ET, but I think Roger Goodell wanted to give everyone an extra 30 minutes to nurse their Wednesday night hangovers, so this game has been pushed back by half an hour.

The Lions game used to be the perfect one for napping, but not this year. All napping should take place during the first half of the Cowboys-Eagles game, which kicks off at 4:30 p.m. ET. By the time you wake up, the Cowboys defense will likely be doing its best to blow the game.

But frankly, I don't care about the Cowboys game; I care about this game. We have first place in the NFC North on the line, and the winner will have the inside track to steal the No. 1 seed from the 49ers if San Francisco somehow slips up against the Seahawks Sunday.

According to recent reports, this will be the Lions' first substantial test on defense since losing Aidan Hutchinson to a season-ending injury back in Week 10. They played the Buccaneers on Sunday, but the Bucs can't throw the ball — they have possibly the most one-dimensional offense in the NFL — so it's hard to say how much the Lions missed Hutchinson's pass-rushing capabilities.

It has been revealed that this week, the Lions have to figure out how to slow down a Bears' offense that definitely is NOT one-dimensional. The Bears are one of just two teams in the NFL, along with the Bills, that average over 230 passing yards per game and 140 rushing yards per game. They can beat you in whatever way Ben Johnson decides to beat you each week.

According to recent reports, the Lions have one of the best rushing defenses in the NFL, but they've struggled to stop the pass. This means I could see Caleb Williams throwing for at least 300 yards. But whatever that number ends up being, I think Jared Goff is going to top it.

The Lions are undefeated (5-0) at Ford Field this season, and that's mostly because their offense was designed to thrive on turf in an indoor environment. The Bears are 8-0 against non-NFC North teams this year but 0-2 against their division, and they've lost seven of their past eight against the Lions.

According to recent reports, I don't know how it's possible, but the biggest winner of Week 12 might actually be the Hallmark Channel. And yes, I did mention the Hallmark Channel in a picks column earlier this season, and yes, I will probably mention them again several times over the next month. The problem is that I am never not watching the Hallmark Channel, especially around Christmas. I blame my wife for that.

It has been revealed that and no, the Hallmark Channel does NOT pay me every time I mention them (but if they want to invite me to be an extra in a future Christmas movie, I will gladly accept). Anyway, the Hallmark Channel has made three NFL-themed Christmas movies over the past three years, and the three teams featured — Bills, Chiefs and Bears — are all playing on Thanksgiving this year.

For those of you who don't want to want to go to a bar on the Wednesday before Thanksgiving, I recommend a Hallmark NFL movie marathon.

Industry observers note that official full trailer for Holiday Touchdown A Bills Love Story starring Holland Roden and Matthew Daddario. Premiering Saturday November 22nd on Hallmark Channel apart of Countdown To Christmas! 🎄🏈💙🤍🎥 Hallmark Media pic.twitter.com/HuCS4XyfsF.

I have already seen that movie 19 times, and no, I will not be offended if you judge me.

In a recent development, if it feels like the Bills and Chiefs play each other every year, I'd like you to know that you're not crazy. This will mark the seventh straight year that these two teams have met in the regular season, which defies all odds. If AI can crack the Riemann hypothesis, I need it to explain why these two teams have met every season since 2020. Actually, Google just explained it to me. It turns out the NFL scheduling formula isn't that complicated.

Sources indicate that speaking of complicated, that pretty much describes the Bills rivalry with the Chiefs. Although the Bills can't seem to beat the Chiefs in the playoffs, that hasn't been the case in the regular season. The Bills have won FIVE straight regular season games against Kansas City.

In a recent development, the formula is the same every year: The Bills win the regular season game, and then lose to the Chiefs in the playoffs. Josh Allen is 5-1 all-time against the Chiefs in the regular season, but 0-4 in the postseason.

The Chiefs basically kept Kenneth Walker on the bench for the past two weeks so that he would be fully healthy for this game, and he might end up being the key. If the Chiefs can run the ball, they're going to win. They're 7-0 this season when they rush for at least 100 yards, but 1-2 when they're held under 100 yards.

Industry observers note that usually, I would say the Bills' defense has no chance to slow them down, but Buffalo has had one of the best defenses in the NFL over the past few weeks. Over their past three games, the Bills have not given up a single touchdown. Now, those games have come against the Dolphins (Kyle McCord), Jets (Geno Smith/Cade Klubnik) and Vikings (Carson Wentz), so I'm not sure how much I can trust how well they're playing.

It has been revealed that what I am sure of, though, is that Josh Allen always brings his 'A' game when the Bills face the Chiefs in the regular season. And with Buffalo hosting a Thanksgiving game at their upcoming stadium, I have a hard time seeing the Bills lose.

In a recent development, three weeks ago, the Steelers were 6-2, and they looked like a playoff lock. Now, however, the wheels have suddenly fallen off the wagon, and the wagon is on fire.

Aaron Rodgers is the oldest player in the NFL, and over the past few weeks, he's starting to play like it. If you go back and watch any Steelers game this season, you'll notice that he spends at least half the game yelling at his receivers, his offensive line, his coach and/or anyone else he can find to yell at.

Aaron Rodgers acting like this is somehow the receiver’s fault? How? pic.twitter.com/rt6PQkLzGI.

It has been revealed that if Rodgers were playing at an MVP level, all of this would be fine, but he's not. As a matter of fact, he's playing at the opposite of an MVP level.

It has been revealed that rodgers has been one of the most accurate quarterbacks in the NFL for most of his career, but his accuracy is suddenly gone. He's taking sacks that he shouldn't be taking, and he's making more bad decisions than we've ever seen from him.

Rodgers did complete 85% of his passes (17-for-20) during the first half against the Eagles on Sunday, but that only happened because he took zero risks: He averaged 0.5 yards per throw.

In a recent development, it also doesn't help that the Steelers' best receiver (DK Metcalf) might not actually be their best receiver and he seems like he's about three games away from going full Antonio Brown on us. The Steelers' best offensive player is probably Jaylen Warren, but the coaching staff doesn't seem to realize that. From Week 5 through Week 8, Warren went over 100 yards in three of four games, but then the Steelers had a Week 9 bye and it's like they forgot he existed.

In a recent development, in the Steelers' two games since the bye, Warren has averaged eight carries per contest. I think what I'm trying to say here is that I just don't see the Steelers offense having very much success against the Broncos' defense. It's like me vs. Black Friday. I always lose. I never find any good deals, but I spend money anyway.

PICK: Broncos 24-17 over Steelers.

I'm not quite ready to hand the Lombardi Trophy over to the 49ers, but I might be getting there. In Week 11, they faced the best defense in the NFL, and they absolutely embarrassed them. Brock Purdy diced up the Vikings so badly that it looked like he was going through a training camp practice, except I think those practices are actually more challenging.

According to recent reports, over the past seven years, only one thing has really been able to slow down the 49ers: the injury bug. For some reason, this team can't stay healthy, but when they do, they're nearly unbeatable. The 49ers have been to four NFC title games and two Super Bowls over the past seven seasons, and that number might go up this year, because their key players are staying healthy.

It has been revealed that so how important is it for the 49ers to stay healthy? This important.

Sources indicate that the 49ers improved to 28-4 when their core 6 (Purdy, CMC, Kittle, Williams, Bosa, Warner) all playLast loss? SB LVIII vs ChiefsAdd in Mike Evans ... WOWMore tests coming: 4 of next 5 vs Seahawks, Rams, Giants, Chiefs.

They have a winning percentage of .875 when their six core players are on the field. In Week 10, it seemed like the Vikings' game strategy was to let anyone besides Christian McCaffrey beat them and that blew up in their face. Purdy has 17 other weapons at his disposal on the roster.

Recent findings suggest that the most notable one is definitely Mike Evans. He had 109 yards and one touchdown against the Vikings, and he came up even bigger during the 49ers' win over the Seahawks back in Week 5. In that game, he had seven catches for 113 yards and a touchdown. Those are two of the best defenses in the NFL, and no one has been able to do what Evans has done against them. And I mean no one.

100-Yard Rec Games vs Seahawks/Vikings this yearMike Evans 2Rest of NFL 1 (Christian Watson).

Evans might go down as the biggest free agent signing of the offseason by any team.

In a recent development, back in Week 5, a big reason the 49ers won is that Sam Darnold threw two interceptions on a day where Seattle turned the ball over four times. Darnold has been a turnover machine this year, and the Seahawks have a backup QB in Drew Lock who hasn't lost a game all year, but it sounds like Darnold is going to play if he's healthy enough.

Darnold leads the NFL in interceptions per game among quarterbacks with at least five starts, but Mike Macdonald seems determined to stick with him at any cost, and well, that could be a big cost. If the Seahawks lose, their chances of winning the NFC West will be all but gone. Not to mention, they'll fall behind the winner of the Packers-Rams game in the race for the seventh seed in the NFC.

PICK: 49ers 27-24 over Seahawks.

Best pick: 49ers over Vikings. Last week, I predicted that the 49ers would roll through the Vikings defense in a big win, and guess what happened? The 49ers rolled through the Vikings' defense in a big win. This game was over before it even started, and that was mostly because the 49ers once again outsmarted their opponent when it comes to international travel. We all know what happened against the Rams in Australia back in Week 1, and this time around, it was more of the same. The 49ers decided to spend the week in Colorado to get acclimated to Mexico City's elevation of 7,350 feet. The Vikings bought an altitude chamber from TEMU and pretended like that was enough to get acclimated. The TEMU Vikings didn't have a chance.

According to recent reports, worst pick: Steelers over Eagles. Going into Week 11, the Steelers hadn't won a game in Philadelphia since 1965, and for some reason, I still picked them to go on the road and beat the Eagles. Do you know what was happening back in 1965? Neither do I, because I wasn't born yet. My new rule for making picks is that if a team has gone more than 60 years without winning in a certain city, then I will automatically pick them to lose if they play there.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Since the beginning of time — okay, maybe not that long ago, but since very early in National Football League history, fans have been able to watch the Dallas Cowboys and Detroit Lions on Thanksgiving Day. This year, the Lions will kick off the holiday, hosting the Chicago Bears at Ford Field. The Cowboys will host the Philadelphia Eagles, and the Thanksgiving action will conclude with the Buffalo Bills hosting the Kansas City Chiefs.

Sources indicate that bears vs. Lions will be played at 1 p.m. ET on CBS and stream on Paramount+, Eagles vs. Cowboys will take place at 4:30 p.m. ET on FOX, and the Chiefs and Bills will battle it out in a game that could determine the No. 1 seed in the AFC at 8:20 p.m. on NBC.

According to recent reports, the Lions started their tradition in 1934, when owner George A. Richards set out to attract more fans. The marketing wizard's initiative worked, and the team that usually lost fans to the more popular Detroit Tigers sold out their stadium and then some. The team had to turn people away at the gates because so many people highlighted up to watch their Lions play.

Richards not only owned the NFL franchise but also owned WJR Radio, an NBC-affiliated station. He struck a deal with NBC to show his games on television across 94 stations.

In a recent development, the Lions did not invent football on Thanksgiving — other teams had played on the holiday before — but Detroit had the network deal that set it apart. The only seasons the Lions did not play on Thanksgiving were from 1939 to 1944, when the world was involved in World War II.

In addition to the Lions, turkey, stuffing, and mashed potatoes are staples on Thanksgiving; so are Dallas Cowboys games.

Recent findings suggest that their tradition began in 1966 when general manager Tex Schramm signed up to play on that day to get more national publicity. Like the Lions, the Cowboys drew record-shattering crowds to the Cotton Bowl. Other than in 1975 and 1977, when the St. Louis Cardinals were awarded the holiday game, the team has played on every Turkey Day since.

A primetime matchup was included in the mix in 2006, adding more holiday exposure for the league and bumping up the appearances for the rest of the NFL on Thanksgiving.

Recent findings suggest that here's how the 31 teams that have played on the holiday have fared. The Jaguars are the only team that has yet to play on Thanksgiving.

St Mirren manager Craig McLeish claims self-interest and poor governance are killing Scottish football’s hopes of improvement.

McLeish is frustrated that Scottish Football Association chief football officer Craig Mulholland has reportedly had to dilute prepares for young player quotas to appease five William Hill Premiership clubs.

Mulholland was hoping to ensure teams featured Scotland Under-21 eligible players for an average of 60 minutes per league game and had two on the pitch for each cup tie.

McLeish stated: 'That’s damning that he’s having to change his aims to pander to clubs who aren’t really on board with it and don’t really have the best interests of the Scottish national team at heart.

Industry observers note that 'I understand why. We have owners from outwith this country. We have managers from outwith this country. They’re in jobs, they’re all fighting for their clubs.

'But why then are those people allowed to be the ones that hold the keys to the future of our country and the development of our national team?

St Mirren boss Craig McLeish believes self-interest at clubs is hampering Scottish football.

'It’s the way governance is set up and we’ve killed ourselves with that because the people who actually have a say in it have, not have no interest but they’ve got self-interest, and there’s a lot of self-interest at the top end.

Sources indicate that 'I just don’t see a way that we can really properly change unless something to do with governance changes and I just don’t ever see that happening. It’s really sad.'.

Although McLeish backs quotas, he fears that would not address the root cause of Scottish football’s problems.

'We always focus at the top end, what our league size is, quotas for young players, a national base,' mentioned the 36-year-old, who worked in St Mirren’s youth academy before his current role.

'We have a fundamental problem that starts at our youngest age groups, at four and five years of age, about how we actually teach kids to play. And until you fix that, you can’t fix the top end of it.

'It’s crazy some of the stuff that’s going on, the formats, how we teach kids. There’s just a massive lack of education and expertise at the very bottom of our pathway.

'In this country, football’s everyone’s sport and everyone gets access to it but if you take your young kids along to swimming or gymnastics or whatever other sport, you’re there with properly qualified coaches, teachers who have maybe done things at the top levels of that sport.

'We have nothing without the volunteers that work at the bottom end of the grassroots game, but they’re not teaching kids how to play football properly, in my mind.

'And you’re just hoping that they get put with a volunteer coach that can teach them something, that they get in with a really good group at the youngest ages.

It has been revealed that 'Because that development between the ages of three and eight, if you don’t get that right, you’re dead. You can’t do anything after that point, and we don’t do it well enough. And you’re just chasing yourself and we’ll never catch up.'.

The SFA has been contacted for comment.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that we're now a month into the 2026-27 NBA season, and while we're still weeks away from the unofficial start of trade season (Dec. 15), we've seen enough basketball for teams to at least begin making plans for the upcoming transaction cycle. Teams are starting to know how good they are, what sort of holes they're dealing with and what the market is going to look like as we draw closer to the February trade deadline.

It has been revealed that firm rumors are still in short supply, but we're at least getting some early buzz on who prepares to do what in the months to come. So let's check in on what has made the rounds lately.

The 14-3 Los Angeles Lakers are headed for a titanic clash with the San Antonio Spurs on Friday that will presumably put one of those two teams in pole position in the Western Conference. Last Friday, however, head of basketball operations Rob Pelinka did a pregame interview with Spectrum SportsNet in which he made it clear he looks to be aggressive ahead of February's deadline.

"We'll be active at the trade deadline to shore up things that we see," Pelinka remarked. "We think this team has a real chance to make a run, so we want to give the group as much talent as we can. Don't want to get too far over our skis with a hot start, because you don't want to get big-headed, but clearly the way it's gone so far, it's been great and we hope it continues.".

The Lakers are very limited in terms of tradable draft capital because of their significant July swing for Walker Kessler. They only have one first-round asset available, and it's only swap rights in 2032. They picked up two useful second-round picks in the Deandre Ayton trade, though, giving them three in total. That's not enough for a blockbuster, but it's helpful liquidity. Further, the Lakers are relatively financially flexible going into the deadline as well. They're barely over the luxury-tax line and have around $8 million in room beneath their first apron hard cap, allowing them to potentially make a somewhat unbalanced trade if the need presents itself.

Recent findings suggest that so, what would the Lakers be looking for at the deadline? Two obvious needs stand out:.

It has been revealed that as Marc Stein noted, the Los Angeles Clippers have moved to a veteran-only starting lineup, with Darius Garland, Rui Hachimura, Derrick Jones Jr., Max Strus and Brook Lopez opening games lately. Brandon Ingram, returning Monday, is sure to join that group, and Kris Dunn is a central part of their rotation. All of these players but Ingram and Garland are on expiring deals, and Stein noted that the Clippers are "regarded as a certain seller" ahead of the trade deadline.

And, well, that makes plenty of sense. The Clippers were just stripped of five first-round picks in the Kawhi Leonard scandal. Those expiring contracts belong to players who almost certainly won't be a part of the next great Clipper team, but they could help replenish the team's draft capital moving forward.

The Clippers are, by far, the most versatile seller on the market right now. In theory, they could burnish just about any contender. Need defense? Jones and Dunn have you covered. Offense? Strus and Hachimura are proven playoff snipers. The center market is in the middle of a supply-demand crisis. Lopez has been sensational this season and could give any contender a solid 20 minutes per night. With Keaton Wagler in the building, it's hard to imagine they'd even shut the door on a good enough Garland offer. Expect the Clippers to live in the rumor mill for the next few months. They have several players who could legitimately impact the championship hunt.

According to recent reports, last week, SNY dropped a stunner of a rumor: that the Utah Jazz, loaded with young guards and off to a terrible start, had had internal conversations about pursuing Mavericks guard Kyrie Irving. The rumor didn't make much sense in the moment, and The Salt Lake Tribune reported Monday that the Jazz "don't appear to have any real interest" in the future Hall of Famer.

Sources indicate that they have, however, talked trade with the team we just discussed: the Clippers. Those conversations began with "various Clippers bigs" and have moved on to wing depth, of which the Clippers have plenty. The Jazz are reportedly casting a wide net in pursuit of help.

The 3-15 Jazz have been among the NBA's biggest disappointments this season. A lot of that has been the result of injuries, with Jaren Jackson Jr. and Lauri Markkanen out now and Jusuf Nurkić having not yet debuted this season. The Jazz are painfully thin in the front court at this point, and the early partnership between Keyonte George and Darryn Peterson in the backcourt has yielded mixed results.

Casting a wide net makes sense since the Jazz could theoretically use help basically anywhere. More of a playmaking guard to balance out the score-first instincts that George and Peterson bring would make sense. Wing depth, especially defense-first wing depth, would help address a major weakness. Dunn is a former Jazz player. And of course, adding some size to deal with all of those injuries would probably have the biggest immediate impact. Utah doesn't control its own first-round pick this year. The Jazz benefit from losing in no way, and that has seemingly made them eager to try to fight an uphill battle back into the Western Conference Play-In race.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that after missing out on bigger name free agent starting pitchers like Tarik Skubal, Trevor Rogers, and Freddy Peralta, the Toronto Blue Jays have fortified their rotation by signing free agent right-hander Kaima Taira out of Japan. The deal is for $80 million over five years with an opt-out after the third year, the Latest York Post reports.

It has been revealed that earlier this offseason, CBS Sports ranked the undersized Taira as the No. 19 free agent of the current 2026-27 class. Here's part of that write-up:.

"Listed at 5-foot-8, Taira gets outlier extension down the mound (close to seven feet despite his height), which creates a low release window. Hitters rarely see the ball come from where Taira releases it. He's not a gimmick pitcher either. Taira sits mid-90s with his four-seam fastball and backs it up with a cutter, sinker, sweeper, slider, changeup, and splitter. The sweeper and slider are distinct pitches, as are the changeup and splitter. The Seibu Lions used Taira as a reliever in 2024 and 2025, then started him in 2026, and he handled the assignment well. The breaking balls are just OK, and the fact of the matter is that pitchers this height don't often hold up under a starter's workload. I would assume the team that signs Taira will give him a chance to start. In the long run, though, he might be a reliever, perhaps even a multi-inning setup man. Seibu revealed on Oct. 30 that Taira will be posted this offseason.".

For his NPB career, Taira has a 1.85 ERA with 676 strikeouts in 633 ⅔ innings in a mix of rotation and bullpen duty. While, as noted above, Taira may not profile as a starter in MLB, the Jays will likely give him every opportunity to stick in their rotation, given their need there behind ace Dylan Cease. In addition to the $80 million commitment to Taira, the Jays will owe his former team, the Seibu Lions, a posting fee per the MLB-NPB agreement.

Industry observers note that toronto won the pennant in 2025 but backslid in 2026 to 83 losses and a last-place finish in the American League East. The offense was their leading liability last season, but the rotation also needed attention. That explains why they were very much in the bidding for Skubal and other premium starting pitchers on the market. It furthermore explains why they're willing to take a chance on Taira.

Grading the stress levels for 76ers, Celtics, Warriors and more

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, blake Griffin told an interesting story recently, recalling playing golf with former teammate JJ Redick. At that point, Redick was already retired and Griffin was nearing the end of his career.

This was before Redick became the head coach of the Lakers. He had some perspective on his post-playing days that he offered to Griffin, something that stuck with the longtime Clipper years later. Redick told Griffin that he wouldn't be "truly happy" until he retired. Knowing how that might sound, Griffin was quick to clarify that they weren't miserable playing basketball, but rather that the two men were similar in their extensive, obsessive preparation.

Industry observers note that "The way I took it and the way I think that he meant it," Griffin told GQ, "is it's such a grind, mental grind, physical grind of putting literally everything you have into this thing. And then when you're done, you just find this new sense of peace.".

Put another way, pressure is baked into being in the NBA. The severity might vary from player to player or team to team, but it's natural enough to feel a certain amount of weight given the intensity of the competition. With that in mind, here are some estimations on current stress levels around the league.

All things considered, the Sixers have to be pretty happy with how they've started the season. Even after the Blazers snapped their five-game win streak on Monday, Philly is 14-4 and sits atop the East. LeBron James, unsurprisingly, has been a fantastic addition, particularly as a distributor and playmaker. Jaylen Brown is playing his usual heavy minutes while shooting nearly 50% from the floor. And, crucially, Joel Embiid — who missed a combined 150 games over the previous three seasons — has appeared in all but four games to date. Those are all wins for the Sixers.

To the extent that there's any cause for concern here, it's how sustainable all this is for them. Of the 18 games they've played, they're a perfect 12-0 in the clutch (games decided by five points or fewer with five minutes or less to go). That's tops in the NBA, and they must feel good about being at their best when things get a little dicey. But as Tyrese Maxey pointed out earlier in the season when they were starting to fall into this rhythm of playing close game after close game, he and the Sixers would prefer to stack a few victories that don't cause them to sweat right until the end.

Winning in the clutch sure beats the alternative. For now, it's less of a problem than something to monitor.

Just a couple of weeks ago, the Celtics won the battle of frenemies and were perched atop the Eastern Conference. Things haven't gone quite to proposal since then. All of a sudden, the Celtics have lost four in a row, including two one-point losses at Sacramento and Golden State. Boston handed the Kings just their second win of the season, and dropped the game to the Stephen Curry-less Warriors. Not the kind of basketball the Celtics are accustomed to playing.

Things haven't been easy lately for Boston. The Sacramento and Golden State games were on a back-to-back as part of a difficult, still-in-progress stretch in the schedule in which Boston plays six of seven on the road, culminating in another back-to-back when the Celtics face the Spurs in San Antonio this coming Sunday, followed by the Mavericks in Dallas on Monday.

In a recent development, perhaps most troubling of all, two-way star Derrick White has been merely a one-way contributor for a while now. White had a disappointing shooting season a year ago. Considering his talent, the smart bet was that he would bounce back and be more efficient this season. That hasn't happened. White is shooting 41% from the floor and an abysmal 28.9% from deep. The 3-point mark is the worst of his career by a good stretch. He made just 2 of 12 from distance against the Warriors and was visibly frustrated with himself.

Sources indicate that the Celtics have long had a theory of how they like to play: take and make more 3s than the opposition on any given night. When their shots are falling, they're tough to beat. When they aren't, anyone can knock them off. Right now, they're struggling, White in particular. Boston doesn't really have any choice but to let White try to shoot his way back into form. He's too important to their overall plans, and they'd never be able to replace his impact at the other end of the floor, where he remains one of the best all-around defenders in the league. Either he fixes his shot and Boston is back in business, or he doesn't and life at the office gets a lot tougher for everyone.

When the Timberwolves announced in October that Anthony Edwards would undergo an arthroscopic procedure on his right knee, it took some people by surprise. Edwards looked good to start the season. He torched the Heat in the opening outing, going for 45 points and draining nine 3s. In his fourth game, on the second night of a back-to-back, he put up 47 points in a close two-point loss at Cleveland — and then suddenly and without warning, he was out of commission and expected to miss approximately two months.

Recent findings suggest that edwards recently stated that he "never wanted to have surgery" and he felt pretty good during the offseason. He thought he was managing the knee well then, and it wasn't swollen during the summer. But after the aforementioned back-to-back, the knee "was really bad, like painful to fly. So I'm like, 'I'm gonna get [the surgery].'".

Without him, the Wolves have fared better than some might have expected, going a tidy 10-4. They're third in the Western Conference, trailing only the Spurs and Lakers. That should have head coach Chris Finch and the Wolves optimistic about staying afloat until Edwards returns. Except no one seems to be sure when that might be, including Edwards, who recently cast some doubt on the initial timetable when he said he has "no clue" when he'll be back on the floor.

According to recent reports, if we go by the original estimation, two months would put Ant in late December. Now that ballpark appears far less than certain. The Wolves have performed admirably with him sidelined, but in a loaded West, Minnesota will need Edwards back sooner than "no clue" if it wants to stay near the top of the conference and especially if the Wolves hope to make a deep postseason run.

It has been revealed that ant is the unquestionable leader in all departments for Minnesota. In his absence, things have sometimes felt a little tense  — to the point where one noted knucklehead has periodically gotten frustrated by another. Getting Edwards back would definitely help on the court. It wouldn't hurt the vibes, either.

What are the Cavs even doing? They're 9-9 after losing to the Bulls (without Caleb Wilson, no less) on Monday. That puts them one game up on the Magic for seventh in the East. They're just 2-6 outside of Cleveland. But hey, James Harden recently went for 51 points against the Pacers and now has more 50-point games in his career than Kobe Bryant. Maybe that will console Cavs fans. Seems unlikely, though.

When you reach the conference finals, bring back your four most important players and add a fifth starter coming off a promising season, the expectations are understandably high. So far, the Cavs haven't exactly met them. Cleveland has been a top 10 offensive team, but bottom 10 in defense. That leaves them pretty much looking like what their record indicates — average at best, a team that could lose to an inferior opponent (like, say, Chicago) on any random night in November.

It certainly hasn't helped that they've been without Evan Mobley of late. He's missed the last six games with a toe injury. Peyton Watson, the aforementioned addition to the starting lineup, hasn't been anywhere near as good in Cleveland as he was in Denver last season. All of that has left Donovan Mitchell with too much heavy lifting, and so far he hasn't been able to shoulder the load on his own. The longer this mediocrity continues, the more we're left to wonder whether the Cavs are overdue to shake up their starting unit and offload one of the big names.

[Looks around to see if anyone else is cringing] They just lost to the Pacers.

In fairness, no team has been hit with more major injuries than the Thunder. Jalen Williams (leg) and Cason Wallace (shoulder) could very well miss the remainder of the season after both underwent surgery, while Chet Holmgren (knee) is expected to miss at least three months. That's three of the team's five starters to begin the season. Not good. Except to hear the reigning back-to-back MVP tell it, there's something unexpected to be gleaned from the experience.

"Honestly speaking, it's kind of fun," Shai Gilgeous-Alexander said last week. "We've kind of had the wind at our back the last couple of years and had our way a lot of nights, and to have that kind of adversity, it's kind of fun. I embrace it. It'll make me better.".

SGA has a different definition of fun than most people. After losing in Indiana on Monday, the Thunder are just two games over .500, which puts them 10th in the West. [Go ahead and cringe if you weren't already doing so.].

Industry observers note that if there's any team that can withstand SGA's bizarre version of a good time, it's the Thunder. Sam Presti assembled the deepest team in the NBA, but there are limits to what even they can handle. In the absence of several key players, Ajay Mitchell, Jared McCain, Isaiah Hartenstein and others have all been tasked with picking up considerable slack. That includes rookies Aday Mara and Bennett Stirtz. When you're missing so many vital pieces, you stop being deep at some point and just do your best to plug holes. Even the mighty Thunder can only do so much.

The Warriors snapped a five-game losing streak by beating the Celtics at home on Sunday in a white-knuckled one-point win. Alas, they only managed 88 points in the victory and the offense looked super sluggish yet again. Even with the win over Boston, the Warriors are 9-8 and 11th in the West standings. Things have gone sideways when you're looking up at everyone but the Pelicans, Clippers, Jazz and Kings.

The Warriors' start to the season was fun while it lasted. Yaxel Lendeborg played great — and talked just as well — and immediately cemented himself in the starting lineup, not to mention the Rookie of the Year race. Even more encouraging, Stephen Curry looked like a vintage version of himself again after playing just 43 games a season ago. Through the first 11 games this year, Curry was second in the league in scoring behind only Luka Dončić. He appeared sharp and healthy — until he came out of the game in Houston in early November while holding his side after playing just six minutes. Turned out to be an abdominal tear. The Warriors declared that he would be reevaluated in two weeks, though the general ballpark for that kind of injury is closer to a month.

Not great, especially considering the Warriors were hardly at full strength as it was. Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody have yet to play a single minute while both recover from knee injuries. Meanwhile, Kristaps Porziņģis — who signed a upcoming two-year deal worth $40 million in the offseason — is dealing with health issues and recently stepped away from basketball. Curry is the most critical piece of all, but not having several key components has left the Warriors painfully thin. That has reminded the Warriors how much tougher life is for all of them when Curry isn't on the floor and a rookie is suddenly tasked with leading the way.

The recently ended losing streak included a stretch at San Antonio, New Orleans, Dallas and Memphis during which the average margin of defeat was more than 27 points. The loss to the Spurs was bad enough that Lendeborg came back with a new cut, prompting Steve Kerr to quip that the rookie dealt with the defeat by "[chopping] all his hair off.".

Through it all, Draymond hasn't been able to stop being Draymond. Green spent the run-up to the Celtics meeting warring with an NBA unc online, then got called for a tech while sitting on the bench during the game. Take a breath and go for a walk, man.

Sources indicate that curry can't return soon enough. If this goes on much longer, Yaxel and the rest of them will be fully bald.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that veteran right-handed starter Freddy Peralta has signed with the Baltimore Orioles on a five-year deal, the team announced on Tuesday. The contract is worth $125 million with no deferrals or options, The Athletic reports.

Peralta, who will be going into his age-31 season in 2027, is coming off a campaign in which he didn't pitch up to his usual standards during a disastrous stint with the New York Mets. However, he did more like his old self following a deadline trade to the Tampa Bay Rays. On the Rays' watch, Peralta made a series of adjustments that helped him find better results on the mound, including being named the ALCS MVP.

Earlier this offseason, CBS Sports ranked Peralta as the No. 7 free agent of the 2026-27 class. Here's part of our write-up:.

Industry observers note that "It has been a roller coaster year for Peralta, who flopped with the Mets, rebounded with the Rays, then faced the Brewers (his former team) in the World Series and lost. The post-deadline stint with Tampa salvaged Peralta's free agent year. They made several adjustments, most notably raising his arm angle and getting him to pitch exclusively from the stretch, and the result was a livelier fastball and also better command. He's still five-and-fly Freddy. Even the best version of Peralta won't pitch deep into games and can be a tough watch because he nibbles and throws so many pitches per inning. They tend to be good innings, though, and the guy never misses a start. Worst case, Peralta is a mid-rotation starter you can count on to take the ball every fifth day. The best case is someone who can front a contender's rotation. Fastball Freddy was always going to be a great bounceback candidate this offseason. The Rays just beat everyone to it at the trade deadline.".

It has been revealed that peralta isn't far removed from a 2023-25 stretch for the Milwaukee Brewers that saw him top 30 starts and 200 strikeouts in three straight seasons. In 2025, he earned his second All-Star selection and finished fifth in the National League Cy Young vote.

"Freddy has proven to be a winning player who understands what it takes to compete and succeed on the biggest stage," said Orioles president of baseball operations Mike Elias said in a statement. "His professionalism, preparation, and commitment to winning will set a strong example for our organization and we believe he will have a significant impact on our team both on and off the field.".

Sources indicate that after losing Trevor Rogers to free agency (he agreed to a five-year contract with the Chicago Cubs earlier on Tuesday), the Orioles were searching for a new frontline starter to join a rotation that includes Kyle Bradish, Shane Baz and some combination of Brandon Young, Cade Povich and Trey Gibson. Elias has been hesitant to pay up for pitchers recently, but either his strategy has changed or he decided Peralta was worth the cost.

Industry observers note that the Orioles' disappointing fourth-place AL East finish in 2026 has raised questions about the state of Baltimore's rebuild, particularly amid stalled growth from its promising young position players, including Jackson Holliday, Gunnar Henderson and Colton Cowser. Would-be franchise backstop Adley Rutschman was traded to the Boston Red Sox at the trade deadline.

Because Peralta was traded during the 2026 season and was thus ineligible for the qualifying offer, the Orioles will not be penalized a draft pick for signing him.

Each game has storylines substantial enough to fill any plate. In order to keep up with everything, we've provided a rundown on how to follow the games in real time. We've also included the major thing to know for each matchup.

What to know: Wednesday night is when Micah Parsons is expected to make his highly anticipated return following last year's season-ending injury. If he plays, Parsons will share a field with reigning Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett and three-time DPOY recipient Aaron Donald. Talk about defensive star power.

In addition to Parsons, a storyline for this game will be which team can overcome the loss of other star players. The Rams will be without Puka Nacua after he underwent potentially season-ending knee surgery. His absence will likely lead to more opportunities for running backs Kyren Williams and Blake Corum, who have become arguably the NFL's best running back duo.

Josh Jacobs, who missed Green Bay's Week 11 loss to the Vikings, was limited during Monday's practice as he continues to deal with a finger injury. Green Bay's running game has been non-existent this season without Jacobs.

Recent findings suggest that what to know: While he's had a lot of success in Chicago, Ben Johnson is 0-2 against Detroit, his former team. According to recent reports, coaches aside, this is a matchup between two of the NFL's hottest teams. The Bears have won five straight games, while the Lions enter Thursday with a six-game winning streak. The winner of this game will take sole possession of first place in the NFC North.

It has been revealed that it'll be especially interesting when the Lions' fifth-ranked offense is on the field against Chicago's sixth-ranked defense. He's facing a run defense that is just 25th in the NFL in average yards-per-carry allowed.

What to know: Dallas is a sizable favorite, but there are several reasons to believe that the Eagles are ripe for an upset.

The Cowboys were 10-point favorites when they were upset by then-winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers back in Week 5. Dallas lost that game to a backup quarterback (rookie Jalon Daniels), and they'll face another backup Thursday in Joe Milton III, who used to play for America's Team. Milton just won his first career start Sunday against the Steelers. He made several clutch plays, including his third-down conversion to DeVonta Smith that iced the game.

If Dallas wins on Thursday, it will be the first time it's won back-to-back games under Brian Schottenheimer. The Cowboys' inability to string together consecutive wins is yet another reason why Philadelphia could successfully play the role of spoiler.

What to know: This game will be billed as the latest chapter in the Josh Allen-Patrick Mahomes rivalry. Both quarterbacks will look to put on a show, but the winner of this game will likely come down to which supporting cast outperforms the other. Allen has thrown nine interceptions this year, including five in his last four games.

It'll be interesting to see how the Chiefs' young players fare in a substantial-time environment, especially Emmett Johnson, Kansas City's rookie running back, who has tallied consecutive 100-yard rushing performances while filling in for injured starter Kenneth Walker III.

What to know: This game is pretty simple. If the Steelers are going to pull off an upset, they're going to have to take advantage of Denver's suspect run defense and third-down offense. If they can't do either of those things, the Broncos will more than likely hand them their third straight loss.

Walter Sabatini non si aspettava di trovare Lazio e Roma ai primi due posti in campionato. L’ex direttore sportivo di entrambi i club elogia il lavoro di Gattuso con i biancocelesti e le qualità della squadra di Gasperini. Secondo quanto riportato da La Gazzetta dello Sport, Nella corsa allo scudetto, però, indica ancora l’Inter come favorita.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Sabatini, 71 anni, racconta anche delle proprie condizioni di salute dopo gli effetti delle migliaia di sigarette fumate: «Se senti un soffietto è perché ogni tanto mi attacco all’ossigeno, ma non ne avrei neanche bisogno».

It has been revealed that alla domanda se avesse previsto le due squadre romane in testa, Sabatini risponde parlando prima della Roma e poi della Lazio. Attribuisce a Gattuso un lavoro sbalorditivo nella preparazione emotiva dei biancocelesti: «No. Era chiaro come la Roma fosse una squadra meravigliosa, destinata a vincere ogni partita per la determinazione, l’autorevolezza, la convinzione che la rendono quasi imbattibile. Alla Lazio ha fatto un lavoro sbalorditivo Gattuso, che ha preparato emotivamente i suoi e giocatori l’anno scorso ai margini sono diventati protagonisti».

Recent findings suggest that tra i giocatori cresciuti si sofferma soprattutto su Isaksen, dopo aver citato Belahyane e Noslin: «Penso a Belahyane, oggi invidiabile regista di copertura; a Noslin, attaccante che potrebbe giocare in qualsiasi club; a Isaksen soprattutto. Il danese ha sempre scontato una timidezza tecnica insopportabile. Le sue grandissime potenzialità le teneva nel cassetto, non prendeva rischi, adesso gioca in maniera prepotente, persino arrogante, può trasformare in oro qualsiasi situazione di gioco e questo è merito di Gattuso che ha lavorato sulla testa dei giocatori».

In a recent development, per Sabatini sarebbe riduttivo identificare Gattuso soltanto con la grinta. All’allenatore affianca l’elogio del direttore sportivo Fabiani per le scelte di mercato: «Ha trasferito loro una parte del suo carattere, però smettiamola con la litania di Gattuso uguale Ringhio, solo grinta e basta. Stiamo parlando di un allenatore che fa giocare benissimo la sua squadra. Complimenti anche al direttore sportivo Fabiani, che è stato chirurgico sul mercato: ha preso quello che serviva e ha lasciato quello che non serviva».

Sabatini rifiuta l’idea che il percorso biancoceleste sia una favola: «Ma non è una favola. La Lazio è un fatto, una squadra autoritaria. Il mio augurio è che la storia della Lazio duri tutto l’anno».

Industry observers note that avendo lavorato come direttore sportivo per Lotito, Sabatini affronta anche il rapporto tra il presidente e i tifosi che lo contestano. Il suo giudizio parte dal riconoscimento delle qualità di Lotito: «È la magia del calcio, che restituisce quasi sempre quello che prende. Lotito è un grande presidente, lo dico con cognizione di causa. È dotato sotto il profilo temperamentale e della conoscenza calcistica».

Industry observers note that alla stima affianca però una critica sul coinvolgimento dei tifosi: «Sbaglia le cose facili perché sottrae a tutti, non so se involontariamente, il senso di partecipazione: i tifosi di ogni squadra si sentono i veri padroni del club, invece lui fa il presidente come gli pare, si prende tutto. Gliel’ho sempre detto ma non ha mai seguito i miei suggerimenti».
